Windows User Guide

Support Assist Tool v0.5.0: Windows User Guide

Detailed procedures for installing, operating, reviewing cases, collecting evidence, and using Support Assist Tool on Windows.

Support Assist Tool 0.5.0
Introduction > About Support Assist Tool

About Support Assist Tool

This guide covers the Windows edition of Support Assist Tool 0.5.0. It describes the controls and workflows available in the Windows application.

SAT separates Engineer Review Workstation work from Customer / Lab Execution Host work. Review features operate on supplied or saved evidence. Local diagnostic and collection tools run only while Customer / Lab mode is enabled for the current SAT session.

Case-centered review

Keep parser state, selected evidence, notes, reports, Health Monitor snapshots, and case-scoped tool sessions associated with the intended case workspace.

Unified Veeam review

Use Auto Detect to review mixed-product evidence without assigning one product identity to an entire bundle.

Universal collection

Detect locally installed Veeam products and gather selected product logs, SAT tool output, and bounded system context through Universal Log Collection.

Focused diagnostics

Run platform-appropriate network, TLS, database, filesystem, VSS, WMI, and Guided Diagnostics on a customer or lab host.

How SAT presents evidence

SAT reports values that it can establish from local state or supplied evidence. When a machine, product, repository, relationship, timestamp, route, certificate identity, or other value cannot be established, SAT reports an unknown or not-identified state. See Product Context and Terminology and Environment Review.

Finding first, component second. In Log Review, the finding describes the symptom. The component identifies where the symptom was reported. For example, Failed to connect to the backup service is the finding; gRPC, transport, repository, VSS, or another component is supporting context. See Reviewing Findings and Symptoms.

Introduction > Windows Requirements and Availability

Windows Requirements and Availability

Use the Windows edition on an approved Windows workstation or on the Windows customer/lab system being diagnosed. The available local diagnostics also depend on the Veeam products and Windows components detected on that machine.

AreaWindows availability
Case selection, Case Dashboard, Log Review, notes and reportsAvailable in Engineer Review.
Environment Review and Health MonitorAvailable with Windows-native system and product data.
File Browser with its Console, and Remote (SSH)Available subject to connection, credential and workspace-role requirements.
TCP/UDP/TLS, RPC, gRPC, SMB and throughput diagnosticsAvailable from Network Tools when the operation applies to the current system.
SQL, VSS, Registry, WMI and VBR diagnosticsAvailable when the required Windows/Veeam components or product role are present.
Log Collection and Guided DiagnosticsProduct-aware. Detected products and applicable diagnostics determine the available choices.
Execution-host boundary. Local diagnostic execution is intended for Customer / Lab mode on the machine being tested. Engineer Review is intended for case analysis and retained evidence.

Runtime package

The Windows portable package uses the SAT Windows dependency model and is distributed as an approved package by your organization. Run SAT from a trusted location and keep the package intact.

Related topicsDownloading and Updating SATWorkspace RolesTools Overview

Will it run here

RequirementDetail
Operating systemWindows 10, Windows 11, or Windows Server 2016 or newer, x64
InstallationNone. Copy the executable on, run it, delete it. No installer, no service, no registry footprint of its own.
Third-party softwareNone required. The Windows build links its dependencies statically, so there is no Visual C++ redistributable or .NET runtime to install first.
PrivilegesRuns as an ordinary user. Servicing-package inventory and some diagnostics need an administrator; where that happens SAT says which reading was skipped and carries on. Unelevated is usually the right choice on a customer machine.
DiskOnly what you point it at. Cases, collections and reports are written where you choose.

Optional third-party tools

A few diagnostics can drive tools that are not part of SAT. Each is optional: without it the related operation reports itself unavailable and everything else keeps working. Integrations shows what was found and where to obtain what was not, so you can place it under your organisation's rules.

ToolUsed for
iPerf3Third-party throughput measurement alongside SAT's own
Wireshark / tsharkPacket capture analysis
SQLCMDSQL Server queries for plug-in cases
Process MonitorFile and registry activity tracing
Packet Monitor (pktmon)Packet capture using the built-in Windows component
ETL2PCAPNGConverting an ETL capture to pcapng for Wireshark
VSS TraceShadow-copy provider tracing

Which local diagnostics apply also depends on what is on the machine: VSS, registry, WMI, SQL and VBR operations appear when the Windows component or Veeam role they read is present, and report themselves as not applicable when it is not.

Introduction > Downloading and Updating SAT

Downloading and Updating SAT

Download the Windows SAT package from your organization’s approved distribution point. SAT has no update check. A newer build comes from your organization's distribution point.

Updating SAT replaces the application only. Case workspaces live outside the application folder and are not touched by an update.

To update SAT within the 0.4.x line, do the following:
  1. Close every running SAT instance and wait for collection, capture, review, or diagnostic work to finish.
  2. Do not delete registered case workspaces, saved reports, notes, or evidence when replacing the executable.
  3. Keep a copy of the existing SAT application directory until the replacement has been verified.
  4. Install or extract the approved Support Assist Tool 0.5.0 Windows package into the intended application location.
  5. Start SAT and click the version in the status bar, or open Help > About SAT. Confirm the displayed product version is 0.5.0.
  6. Open the Active Case selector and confirm that the expected registered cases are available.
  7. Open one important case and verify its saved review/note/report data before retiring the older application copy.
Expected result. The updated Windows application opens while case-owned data remains intact.
Upgrading from 0.3.x. Follow Manual Upgrade. A 0.3.x case layout is not converted automatically.
Related topicsManual UpgradeHelp and F1Release History
Introduction > Manual Upgrade

Manual Upgrade

Use a side-by-side upgrade when moving from a 0.3.x installation to Support Assist Tool 0.5.0. Preserve the original application directory, case directories, logs, notes and reports until the new installation has been verified.

Data to preserve before upgrading

  • The complete older SAT application directory.
  • Every case workspace and original customer log bundle used by the case.
  • Older Logs and State directories.
  • Older Tool-Output or Tool-Outputs directories that contain evidence you still require.
  • Saved reports, case notes and parser/review data that must remain part of the case record.
To manually upgrade from 0.3.x to 0.5.0, do the following:
  1. Close the older SAT instance and make sure no parser, collection, capture or diagnostic task is running.
  2. Back up the complete older SAT application directory and every case workspace stored elsewhere.
  3. Install or extract 0.5.0 into a separate location. Do not delete or overwrite the old copy during verification.
  4. Start 0.5.0. If an older case workspace already contains a case.json that 0.5.0 accepts, choose Register Existing Case and select that compatible workspace.
  5. If a 0.3.x workspace is not accepted as a current case, leave it unchanged. Create a new 0.5.0 case and review the preserved original log bundles/directories in that case. Do not rename or fabricate case metadata to force registration.
  6. If compatible saved structured review data exists in a registered case, use Load saved review to reopen it. Otherwise perform a new review of the preserved source logs.
  7. Open Note Review, existing reports and important evidence and confirm that the case record you need is available.
  8. Only after verification should you retire the older executable directory according to your support-data retention policy.
Expected result. Unsupported 0.3.x data remains preserved as a rollback/reference copy, while 0.5.0 uses its current case layout for new work.

Import Previous SAT Data

The Import Previous SAT Data action checks recognized historical Logs, State, Tool-Output and Tool-Outputs locations beside the current SAT executable. It does not browse arbitrary old installations. Use it only when those historical folders are actually located beside the current executable, and keep the original data until the import has been verified.

No general 0.3.x converter. The Windows application does not provide a universal converter for every historical 0.3.x case layout. Preserve unsupported workspaces and re-review their original evidence in a 0.5.0 case.

Introduction > Workspace Roles

Workspace Roles

SAT has two workspace roles. The role is not stored as a permanent preference. Without an engineer licence SAT starts, and stays, in Customer / Lab Execution Host, whatever is beside the executable. With a licence, a pristine portable copy with no SAT application or case state starts in Customer / Lab Execution Host, and a copy with ApplicationLogs, recognized legacy SAT state, or Cases beside it starts in Engineer Review Workstation.

Feedback in the status bar works with an engineer licence. Without one it does nothing.

RoleUse it forImportant behavior
Engineer Review WorkstationCases, Log Review, parser/evidence work, Environment Review, notes, reports, saved Health snapshots and read-only imported customer evidence.Persistent engineer case/application data is preserved. Customer cleanup rules do not delete the Engineer workspace.
Customer / Lab Execution HostLive Health, Log Collection, network/platform diagnostics, captures, change tools and Guided Diagnostics on the machine being tested.Designed to leave minimal remnants after a successful support bundle. Transient tool/application logs are cleaned only after they are completely archived.

Switching mode from the role indicator

Left-click the role indicator to switch or right-click it for the context menu. If open tool work blocks the transition, SAT lists the blocking work as a Case -> task tree (plus a No Case/standalone branch). You can close work manually, cancel the switch, or choose Close All and Switch. SAT requests normal cancellation/owned-capture stop and changes role only after the blocking work has actually closed.

Startup detection is not a persisted role preference. Copying a pristine SAT build to a customer/lab host is intended to open in Customer/Lab. An engineer installation that already contains SAT state opens in Engineer Review.

Interface Basics

AreaPurpose

Workspace tabs

More than one tool can remain open. A tab can be RUN, FINISHED, or IDLE depending on its current operation state. Closing a running tab requires confirmation; closing idle tabs does not stop tools that belong to another case context.

Where you are

Every page shows its place directly under the title, for example Home > Case Manager. Select Back to return to the previous level.

Resizing and collapsing panes

The panes on these pages are separated by dividers. A divider shows three dots between the panes and becomes a green line under the pointer.

PageDividers
Log ReviewBetween the three overview tables, and between the tables, the Issue Summary and the finding detail.
Environment ReviewBetween the topology and the details, and between those two and the report below them.
Health MonitorBetween the two rows of tables, and down the middle of each row.
Case DashboardBetween the bookmarked evidence and the summaries, and between the two summaries.
IntegrationsBetween the tool catalogue and the selected tool's detail.
File BrowserBetween the folder tree and the folder's contents.
Remote (SSH)Between the file pane and the terminal.
  • Drag a divider to resize the panes on either side. Each pane stops at a minimum size.
  • Collapse a pane by dragging past half of its minimum size. The divider stays at the edge, so the pane can be pulled back out. The Integrations panes, the File Browser contents pane and both Remote panes stop at their minimum size and do not collapse.
  • Double-click a divider to bring a collapsed pane back at its previous size. Double-clicking a divider when neither side is collapsed returns it to its default position.
  • Positions are saved in ui-settings.ini and restored the next time SAT starts. View > Reset Pane Layout returns every divider to its default.

Dropping files and folders on SAT

Drag files or folders from File Explorer onto the SAT window, or onto SupportAssistTool.exe itself.

  • A file opens the File checksum (SHA-256) window, which reads the file and shows its SHA-256, size and folder, as certutil -hashfile does. Files dropped later, on SAT or on the checksum window, join the same list.
  • A folder opens Log Review with Auto Detect on that folder. SAT asks first. With a case active, Yes adds the result to the case, No reviews the folder without adding it, and Cancel does nothing.

Paste a published SHA-256 into Expected SHA-256 to compare it with every file in the list. Letter case and spaces are ignored, so a value from a download page, or from certutil output with a space between each pair of bytes, can be pasted as it is. The line below it names the file that matches, or says that none does. Copy SHA-256 copies the selected values, Copy all copies the list as tab-separated rows, and closing the window stops any file still being read.

Drop a checksum list with the files to check them all at once. A file named SHA256SUMS, with or without a suffix such as SHA256SUMS.txt, or ending in .sha256, .sha256sum or .sha256sums, is read as a list when every line is in the form sha256sum writes or in the form SHA256 (name) = value. A .sha256 file holding a single value gives the value for the file it is named after, so tool.zip.sha256 checks tool.zip. The list adds a Check column, and the line above the table sums up how the files compare with it.

CheckMeaning
Matches SHA256SUMSThe file's SHA-256 is the value the list gives it.
Does not match SHA256SUMSThe file's SHA-256 is not the value the list gives it.
Not foundThe list names the file, and it is not in the list's folder.
Not checkedThe file could not be read, or its name in the list points outside the list's folder.
Not listedNo dropped list names the file.

A list dropped on its own brings in every file it names, looked for beside the list, as sha256sum -c does. A list dropped with files checks those files, matched by name, and adds nothing else. Only files in the list's folder, or below it, are read: a name that is absolute, starts with a drive or a server, or climbs out with .. is shown as not checked and is not opened. Copy all includes the Check column once a list has been dropped.

Only regular files are read, and nothing dropped is run or opened with its own program. When SAT runs as administrator, Windows does not pass it a drop from a File Explorer window that is not running as administrator. From the command line, files hash prints the same values; see the CLI User Guide.

The menu bar

The menu bar runs along the top of the SAT window. Every entry opens a page, a window or an action that the rail and the cards also reach. Press Alt, or the letter underlined in a menu name, to open a menu from the keyboard.

MenuEntries
FileOpen Log-Collections Folder opens the Log-Collections folder beside SAT in File Explorer and creates it when it is missing. Exit closes SAT.
EditCopy (Ctrl+C), Paste (Ctrl+V) and Select All (Ctrl+A) act on the control that has the focus.
GoHome, Case Manager, Case Dashboard, Environment Review, Health Monitor, Log Review, File Browser, Remote (SSH), Tools, Integrations and Recent Activity open the page. Case Manager and Case Dashboard are greyed in Customer / Lab. Jump To... (Ctrl+K) searches for a page, tool, case or command.
ViewRefresh (F5), Full Screen (F11), Running Jobs, Increase Text Size (Ctrl++), Decrease Text Size (Ctrl+-), Reset Text Size (Ctrl+0) and Reset Pane Layout.
ToolsLog Collection, Guided Diagnostics and Network Tools open their Tools pages. The quick tools open in their own windows: Name Check (F2), Local Port Checker (F6), Time Check (F7), File Lock Check (F8), Volume Check (F9), File Transfer Calculator (F10) and Service and Process Watch (F12). Integrations opens the Integrations page and Settings... the Settings window.
HelpUser Guide opens this guide and reads User Guide (missing) when the file is not beside the application. Getting Started, Import Previous SAT Data... and About SAT open their Help articles. See Help and F1.
To open a page from the menu bar, do the following:
  1. Choose Go, then the page, for example Go > Health Monitor.
  2. Choose Tools, then a Tools page or a quick tool, to go there directly.
To fill the screen with SAT and return, do the following:
  1. Choose View > Full Screen, or press F11. The window fills the screen and a button named Exit full screen appears.
  2. Choose Exit full screen, or press F11 again, to return to the window.
To change the text size, do the following:
  1. Choose View > Increase Text Size or press Ctrl++ to enlarge every piece of text by 10 percent, up to 200 percent.
  2. Choose View > Decrease Text Size or press Ctrl+- to reduce it, down to 70 percent.
  3. Choose View > Reset Text Size or press Ctrl+0 to return to 100 percent. The status line shows the scale.
To reset the pane dividers, do the following:
  1. Choose View > Reset Pane Layout. Every divider returns to its default position.
To find a page, tool, case or command with Jump To, do the following:
  1. Press Ctrl+K, or choose Go > Jump To....
  2. Type part of the name. Every word typed must appear in the name or in where it lives.
  3. Press Up or Down to select a row, then Enter to open it. Esc closes the window.
To see the running jobs, do the following:
  1. Choose View > Running Jobs, or click the running time beside Active case.
  2. Select a session and choose Go to Session, or double-click it, to show it. Choose Cancel Job to cancel a running job.

Jump To (Ctrl+K)

Press Ctrl+K, or choose Go > Jump To, to reach a page, a tool, a case or a command by typing part of its name. Every word typed must appear in the name or in where it lives, so net ping finds Ping on Network Tools. Names that start with what you typed come first, then names with a word that starts with it.

  • Enter opens the selected row, Up and Down move through the list, and Esc or a click elsewhere closes it.
  • A page opens the page, a tool opens its session tab as its card does, a case becomes the active case, and a command runs: Running Jobs, Settings, User Guide, Reset Pane Layout or Refresh.
  • In the Remote (SSH) terminal, Ctrl+K goes to the shell, where it erases to the end of the line. Use the Go menu from there.

Running Jobs

View > Running Jobs, or a click on the running time beside Active case, opens a window that lists every session tab in every case: its page, its case, its state and its newest progress report. Running jobs come first, with how long they have run, and the list updates twice a second. A state reads Running with the time, Cancelling, Finalizing output, Finished or Not run.

Go to Session, a double-click or Enter shows the selected session, switching to its case first when it belongs to another. Cancel Job cancels a running job, as its own Cancel button does.

Filtering a results table

Type into Filter rows, on the caption line above a page's results table, to keep in view only the rows with a cell that contains the text. Letter case is ignored. The status line says how many rows match, Esc in the box clears it, and opening another page or session tab shows every row again. Selecting, copying and opening evidence from a filtered row work as they do on the full table.

The same box sits on three more pages. On Health Monitor, on the banner row, it filters the four tables together and keeps filtering as each new sample arrives. On File Browser, at the end of the location row, it filters the folder's contents: the parent folder entry stays, Refresh keeps the filter, and opening another folder clears it. On Environment Review, before the page's buttons, it filters the details grid and shows only while the selected section is a table. Health Monitor and Environment Review say how many rows match on the status line, File Browser on the line below its list, and Esc clears the box.

Cards on a short window

When the window is short, the summary cards on Log Review, Health Monitor, Environment Review and Case Dashboard share one row at a smaller height and show their caption and value, so the tables below them keep their room. A taller window gives the cards their full size and their detail line again.

Introduction > Home

Home

Home is a status board: it answers what is going on before you open anything else. Each role has its own board. A tile shows a count or a state with a line beneath it, and its link opens the page that holds the detail. Left-click the role badge in the header to switch role, or right-click it for the role menu.

Engineer Review

SectionWhat it shows
CASE FLOWThe active case in four steps: 1 CASE (its ID and title, or None with New case), 2 LOGS (the sources added and when they were reviewed), 3 EVIDENCE (the log lines bookmarked or marked for the note; with none kept, the saved review's top finding) and 4 NOTE (whether the #note is saved, a draft or not written).
IN PROGRESSNEXT STEPS written on the Case Dashboard, RUNNING JOBS and CASES by status, with links to Case Dashboard, Running Jobs and Case Manager.
RECENT CASESThe cases opened most recently, then the rest newest first. The active one is marked ACTIVE; a click makes a case the active case. A deleted case leaves the list at once.

The links under the board open New case, Case Manager, Log Review, Environment Review, a health snapshot, Integrations, and Switch to Customer / Lab.

Customer / Lab

SectionWhat it shows
THIS MACHINE'S HEALTHOverall, CPU, memory, paging, storage and network, from Health Monitor's sampler.
FOUND ON THIS MACHINETHIS MACHINE, the VEEAM PRODUCTS found, the GUIDED DIAGNOSTICS that apply to them, and the VEEAM SERVICES and how many run.
THIS SESSIONCOLLECTED (the last log collection), LAST OUTPUT (the newest tool output, with Prepare) and PENDING RESTART (whether the system waits for a restart, with Details).

Below the board: Collect logs, and Prepare output and Delete output once there is output; the QUICK TOOLS row, one link for each quick tool with its key; and OPEN, with Tools, Environment Review, Log Review, Health Monitor and Recent Activity. See Quick Tools.

The board fits its window. On a short window the lower sections show compact, the lowest first, so every section stays in view.

To start a case from Home in Engineer Review, do the following:
  1. Choose New case under the board, or Case Manager to select a case that exists.
  2. Choose Log Review to review logs for the active case. The CASE FLOW tiles follow the case through CASE, LOGS, EVIDENCE and NOTE.
  3. Choose a case under RECENT CASES to make it the active case.
To collect logs from Home in Customer / Lab, do the following:
  1. Choose Collect logs under the board.
  2. When the collection has finished, choose Prepare output to gather this session's output for sending, or Delete output to remove it.
  3. Open a quick tool from the QUICK TOOLS row with its link or its key.

Getting Started > Complete Your First Log Review

Complete Your First Log Review

This procedure covers the normal engineer path from opening SAT to reviewing a supplied Veeam log bundle and preparing evidence for a case note.

To create a case and review logs, do the following:
  1. Start SAT. It opens in Engineer Review Workstation mode.
  2. From Home, select New Case. See Creating a Case.
  3. Enter the case workspace location, case identifier, readable title, and engineer name required by the dialog.
  4. Create the case and confirm that it appears in Active case.
  5. Open Log Review and select Auto Detect Veeam Logs (Recommended).
  6. Add the supplied ZIP bundle, directory, or individual log source. See Adding Logs for Review.
  7. Start the review. If the result is INDEXED: PRELIMINARY, use it to orient yourself and select Complete full review when deeper analysis is required.
  8. Choose the affected machine or leave All Machines selected for an environment-wide view. See Reviewing All Machines.
  9. Select the job/activity and the run that corresponds to the reported time or failure. See Jobs, Activities, and Run History.
  10. Review the finding text first, then severity, time, component, and source evidence.
  11. Add only relevant findings or run details to #note. See Adding Findings to #note.
  12. Open Case Dashboard and select Open case note. Review and copy/save the note as required.
Result. The case retains the review state and the evidence you intentionally selected.

Quick local review on a customer or lab computer

If you need a fast local look and do not need persistent case state, enable Customer / Lab mode, leave Active case at No Case, open Auto Detect Veeam Logs, and use the local-detection option. SAT can identify applicable local Veeam log roots and index them without first creating a case. Choose Custom/manual source selection when the desired logs are outside the detected product paths.

Related topics

Finish a Review with a Case NoteEnvironment ReviewReviewing a Saved Health SnapshotUniversal Log Collection
Getting Started > Finish a Review with a Case Note

Finish a Review with a Case Note

Only the findings and evidence you select go into the case note. The note is built from the evidence you include.

To finish a log review with a note, do the following:
  1. In Log Review, select the machine, job/activity, and run that you want to document.
  2. Add the run findings or settings that are relevant to the case.
  3. Select additional findings only when their source evidence adds useful detail.
  4. If a Health Monitor snapshot is part of the review, add only the Health Monitor rows that are relevant.
  5. Open Case Dashboard.
  6. Select Open case note.
  7. Review the generated sections, including Issue, machine/product information, selected findings, job/activity findings, job settings, related run context, Health Monitor, and evidence.
  8. Edit the note where the interface permits manual review or completion.
  9. Use Copy #note or save a reviewed note snapshot as needed.
Result. The note contains the case evidence you selected, not every parser finding.

Getting Started > How To

How To: Common Support Tasks

Each task below is the short path from a customer symptom to something you can put in a ticket. They assume nothing except that SAT is running.

If the customer says...Start here
"The backup job failed last night."Find why a job failed
"Offload to capacity tier is not working."Investigate a tiering or offload task
"The agent cannot reach the backup server."Prove a connectivity problem
"The SQL plug-in backup fails."Work a database plug-in case
"Here are my logs." (a zip you have never seen)Identify an unfamiliar bundle
"It worked yesterday."Find what changed on the machine
Getting Started > How To

Find Why a Job Failed

  1. Create or select a case. See Creating a Case.
  2. Add the customer's bundle in Adding Logs for Review and leave the profile on Auto Detect.
  3. Let the fast index finish, then open Jobs, Activities, and Run History and select the run that failed. The run list is newest first.
  4. Read the run story at the top of the detail pane. It is the sequence of events for that run, in order, so you can see how far it got before it stopped.
  5. Open Reviewing Findings and Symptoms for the grouped errors, then Reviewing Source Evidence to read the original line in context.
  6. Add what you found with Adding Findings to #note.
If the run list is empty. Fast index reads the high-value logs first. If the run you want is not there, run a Full Review from Fast Index and Full Review before concluding the evidence is missing.
Getting Started > How To

Investigate a Tiering or Offload Task

Offload, archival and retention are tasks. They have no backup job behind them, so looking for a failed job finds nothing.

  1. Add the bundle and let Auto Detect finish.
  2. Check Components Found in the review summary. A repository bundle reports Repo, and a scale-out repository also reports SOBR. If the bundle only reports an agent, you are looking at the wrong machine's logs.
  3. Open Jobs, Activities, and Run History and look at the entries tagged with the owning component, not at backup jobs.
  4. If the evidence points at another host, note the target name in the failing line, then collect from that host as well. See Related Documentation for the collection article that matches it.
Getting Started > How To

Prove a Connectivity Problem

  1. Get the exact target and port from the failing log line. Ports differ by role. Check Used Ports for the role involved.
  2. Run Remote Port Checker from the machine that is failing, to the machine it is failing to reach. Direction matters.
  3. If the connection succeeds but the product still fails, run TLS Handshake to see which protocol and cipher were actually negotiated.
  4. If the customer suspects a firewall between sites, use Testing Across Local Interfaces so you can show which local NIC was used.
  5. Attach the result with Adding Findings to #note. A passing test is as useful as a failing one because it moves the fault elsewhere.
Getting Started > How To

Work a Database Plug-In Case

  1. Establish which mode the plug-in runs in, standalone or managed. This decides where the evidence lives; see Standalone and Managed Operation Modes.
  2. Collect from the database server, not only the backup server. The plug-in runs on the database host and connects out to Veeam Backup & Replication.
  3. Add both bundles to the same case with Appending New Logs to an Existing Case so the timeline lines up.
  4. Use the run story to see how far the session got: the plug-in starting, connecting to the backup server, authenticating, then moving data.
  5. If the plug-in never reached the backup server, the case is a connectivity or certificate problem, not a database problem. Switch to Prove a Connectivity Problem.
Getting Started > How To

Identify an Unfamiliar Bundle

  1. Add it with Auto Detect and let the fast index run.
  2. Read Components Found first. It lists every Veeam component the evidence proves is present, so you learn what the machine actually is before you form a theory about it.
  3. Check the machine list in Reviewing All Machines. A bundle can contain several machines.
  4. Use Environment Review for the installed products, versions and topology.
A bundle can be more than one thing. A backup server that also hosts a repository and has an agent installed reports all three. That is the machine telling you what it is, not SAT being unsure.
Getting Started > How To

Find What Changed on a Machine

  1. Take a capture before the change with System Differences.
  2. Reproduce the customer's action, or wait for the scheduled operation.
  3. Compare against the baseline. The comparison reports what was added, removed and modified.
  4. For an environment you cannot baseline in advance, use Environment Review against a collection taken while the problem was happening.

Working with Cases > Case Manager

Case Manager

Case Manager is the queue of every case SAT can see. It is where a case is created, brought in, opened, updated and deleted. Case Dashboard is where a case is worked once it is open.

Reading the queue

Six cards across the top summarise the queue: the number of registered cases, how many sit in each status, which case is active, and the total evidence gathered across all cases. Evidence is counted from the case folders themselves, so it stays accurate when files are added or removed outside SAT.

The table below lists every case, newest first, with its status shown as a coloured marker. Select a case to act on it, or double-click it to make it active and open its Case Dashboard. Right-click a row for the same actions.

Case status

Each case carries a status you set: Opened, Waiting On Response or R&T. A case created before this build has no stored status and reads as Opened until you change it.

To change a case status, next steps or notes, do the following:
  1. Select the case in the table.
  2. Choose a Status.
  3. Enter Next steps . This is what you or a colleague picking the case up should do next.
  4. Enter Case notes.
  5. Select Save case details.
Result. The details are written to the case workspace and travel with it. Your place in the queue is kept, so you can continue with the same case.
Next steps and case notes belong to the case, not to a review. They are not replaced when logs are re-analysed, and they are readable by anyone who opens the case workspace.

Working with Cases > About Cases

About Cases

A SAT case is the persistent workspace used to keep review state and case-owned evidence together. Log Review can be used without an active case for one-off analysis, but ad-hoc review state is not retained as a case.

When to use a case. Create or select a case when you want SAT to retain log-review state, selected evidence, notes, saved snapshots, or reports across sessions.

Working with Cases > Creating a Case

Creating a Case

To create a new case, do the following:
  1. Open Case Manager and select New case. The form opens on the page.
  2. Confirm or browse to the parent folder where the case workspace will be created.
  3. Enter a unique case or ticket identifier.
  4. Enter a readable case title.
  5. Enter the engineer name.
  6. Leave Create standard logs, captures, reports, baselines, notes and tools folders selected unless you are attaching to an existing folder layout.
  7. Select Create and activate.
Result. SAT creates the case workspace, makes it the Active case, and returns to the queue with the new case selected.

Working with Cases > Selecting or Registering a Case

Selecting or Registering a Case

The Active Case selector is available as part of the main SAT workspace on supported Windows, Linux, and macOS builds. Use it to change the case context without closing and reopening SAT.

Select a known case

To switch the active case, do the following:
  1. Open the Active Case dropdown.
  2. Select the case you want to work with, or select No Case for a non-persistent review/diagnostic context.
  3. Wait for the Case Dashboard and case-aware workspaces to refresh.
Result. New case-owned review actions use the selected case. Tool sessions that belong to another case are hidden and stay with their own case.

Register an existing case workspace

To register an existing case, do the following:
  1. Open Case Manager and select Register / import.
  2. Browse to an existing SAT case workspace, or to a folder that holds several of them.
  3. Confirm the selection.
Result. The case or cases are added to the queue, and the first becomes the Active case. Cases already registered are kept.

Load a saved review without rescanning

Use Load Saved Review to reopen structured parser data already stored in the active case. This is useful when returning to a case after closing SAT and you do not need to parse the original log sources again.

Case-Scoped Tool SessionsAppending New LogsDeleting a CaseManual Upgrade
Working with Cases > Case-Scoped Tool Sessions

Case-Scoped Tool Sessions

Open tool sessions belong to the case context in which they were created. No Case is also a context. Changing the Active case changes which tabs are visible; it does not redirect a running operation to the newly selected case.

To work in several cases without mixing tool state, do the following:
  1. Select No Case and open a TCP / UDP Listener.
  2. Select Case 1 and open Log Review and a TCP test.
  3. Select Case 2. The Case 1 tabs disappear. Any running Case 1 worker continues with its original case/output binding.
  4. Open another tool in Case 2.
  5. Return to No Case. The original listener tab returns with the events it received while it was hidden.
  6. Return to Case 1. Its Log Review and TCP test tabs return with their existing state/results.
Result. Each case and No Case has its own visible tool group while SAT safely owns all running workers in the background.
Tool session limit, and how to raise it. Every tool you open becomes its own tab, bound to the case context you opened it in. SAT allows 15 open tool tabs by default, counted across the whole workspace, so every case you have open plus No Case shares that budget. Closing a case releases the tabs that belonged to it.

To change it, open Tools > Settings > General and set Maximum tool sessions. Any value from 1 to 30 works; anything outside that is clamped to the nearest end. Save applies it immediately, with no restart. When you hit the limit SAT points you at the same setting in the message, so you do not have to come back here for it.

Working with Cases > Case Dashboard

Case Dashboard

The Case Dashboard shows the active case as one Veeam environment: its systems and components, the jobs and runs found in them, and the findings, evidence and notes kept with the case. Use it after a review to pick a system, a job and an exact run, to write the case's note, and to continue the case with more logs.

Before You Begin

  • The Case Dashboard belongs to Engineer Review. In Customer / Lab the page is hidden and its Go menu entry is greyed.
  • Select a case first, on Case Manager or in the header, and review its logs once with Log Review. Until the case holds a review, the page reads "Select a case to load accumulated machines, jobs, findings and evidence."
To open the Case Dashboard and read a run, do the following:
  1. Choose Go > Case Dashboard. The page opens on CASE OVERVIEW, with a card for each metric of the case.
  2. Choose a system or component in System. The list holds the source owners and the related Veeam components and managed workloads found by every parser. Choose ALL Systems / Components for the whole case.
  3. Choose a job or activity in Job / Activity. Backup, Plug-in, Rescan and Activity items are grouped.
  4. Choose a run in Run. A selection of all runs shows a summary and does not pick the first run for you.
  5. Read MACHINE AND PRODUCT, SELECTED JOB RUN and COMPONENTS WITH FINDINGS. Double-click a row to open its source evidence. A warning or error with no source opens a Result Details window.
To write the case note from the dashboard, do the following:
  1. Choose the system, job and run the note is about. ALL Systems / Components opens the master note.
  2. Choose Open case note. The note opens with the selected scope. See Note Review.
  3. Choose Copy #note to copy the note text, or Bookmark evidence to keep the selected evidence line with the case.
To continue a case, do the following:
  1. Choose Load saved review to reopen the review stored with the case. The raw logs are not read again.
  2. Choose Review new logs / append to review later logs and add only the new evidence to the case. See Appending New Logs to an Existing Case.
  3. Choose Re-analyze sources to review the case's saved sources again.
  4. Choose Load tool evidence to load the tool output collected on a Customer / Lab machine into the case.

Buttons

ButtonWhat it does
New caseCreates a case workspace without leaving the dashboard. See Creating a Case.
Load saved reviewLoads the selected case's stored review without scanning the logs again.
Review new logs / appendReviews later logs and appends the new evidence to the active case.
Open case noteOpens the note for the selected system and run, or the master note.
Load tool evidenceLoads the diagnostic tool output collected from a Customer / Lab machine. Each machine is read from the tool manifest, and the evidence is ordered in UTC across machines.
MoreOpens a menu: Re-analyze saved sources, Environment Review, Open master case note, Export selected system / run PDF..., Export master case PDF..., Engineer notes, Open case folder, Open / manage cases, Register existing case..., Load Customer / Lab tool evidence... and Delete active case....

Deleting a case removes its workspace and SAT's references to it after a confirmation, and only when no operation is running for the case. See Deleting a Case.

Panes

A divider separates the bookmarked evidence from the summaries, and the two summaries from each other. Drag it to resize the panes, and double-click it to return it to its default position. See Interface Basics. On a short window the cards at the top share one row.

The dashboard follows the order Log Review uses: a system or component, then a job or activity, then a run.

Case Manager

Adding Your Own Case Statuses

The statuses in the Status dropdown are yours to set, from Tools > Settings > Custom Statuses.

Each row is one status: a colour on the left and the name on the right. + Add status adds a row, Remove deletes one, and Save writes them. The order of the rows is the order of the dropdown, and the first row is the status a new case starts in.

There are 24 colours in the dropdown, each shown as a swatch beside its name. Grey is the default for a status you add without choosing a colour.

The statuses are still stored as text in ApplicationLogs\case-statuses.txt beside the application, so a copy of SAT carries them with it. Editing that file by hand still works, but Settings is the supported route and applies without a restart.

A case already carrying a status you later remove keeps showing it, because a status is stored on the case as text.

To give a case a custom status, do the following:
  1. Choose Tools > Settings... and open the Custom Statuses tab.
  2. Choose + Add status, choose a colour and type the name, then choose Save.
  3. Select the case on Case Manager and choose the status in the Status dropdown.
Case Dashboard

Importing Collections for Several Machines

Environment Review and Health Monitor can rebuild their reports from a raw log collection, and the case remembers what you imported.

On either page choose Open ▾ → Import from a collection folder. Point SAT at one collection, or at a folder holding several collections, and it rebuilds every one it finds and saves them into the active case.

Open ▾ → Import from a collection .zip does the same with the archive a log collection produces, so you do not have to extract it first. A folder holding several collection archives imports all of them. SAT reads the files it needs out of the archive into a temporary directory that it removes before the import finishes, and the case records the archive as the source.

Each machine gets its own folder under reconstructed\ inside the case, listed in an index beside them. Once a case holds more than one machine, Open ▾ → Saved in this case becomes a list to choose from, naming each machine and when it was imported.

Reopening the case restores what it holds, so you do not import again after restarting SAT. Importing a machine that is already in the case replaces its entry and does not add a second one. This is how you bring in a newer collection for a machine you already have.

A rebuilt report is not a live capture, and it says so: each machine's folder carries a note recording which collection it came from and listing everything the collection could not supply.

Interface Basics

What SAT Does While a Long Operation Runs

Collections, reviews, imports and report exports run on a background thread, so the window keeps drawing and tells you where it has got to.

While one of these runs, the rest of the window stops accepting input until it finishes. That is deliberate: it prevents a second action starting against files the first one is still writing.

Only the interface is kept responsive this way, using one background thread. How much of your machine a review uses is a separate question, reported per review as Parser workers. On a machine with few cores a large review takes longer but continues to make progress, and the status line keeps naming the file it is reading.

Working with Cases > Appending New Logs

Appending New Logs to an Existing Case

Use the same case when additional logs arrive later and belong to the same investigation. Appending a new source adds its review data to the existing case and keeps the earlier source.

To append a later log delivery, do the following:
  1. Select the existing case from Active case.
  2. Open Case Dashboard or Log Review.
  3. Select Review New Logs / Append.
  4. Add the new ZIP bundle, folder, or log source.
  5. Use Auto Detect unless a manual parser selection is required.
  6. Run the review.
  7. Return to the case-wide view and confirm that the new machines, activities, runs, or findings appear alongside the previous material.
Result. The case contains both the earlier and later review data.

Deleting a Case

Permanent operation. Deleting a SAT case removes the case workspace and its case-owned evidence. Case evidence stays when the workspace role changes or the application restarts.
To delete a case, do the following:
  1. Finish or cancel any operation that is still writing to the case.
  2. Select the case as Active case.
  3. Choose Delete case on Case Manager, or Delete active case from the More menu on the Case Dashboard.
  4. Read the confirmation message.
  5. Confirm deletion only when the case workspace is not needed again.

Log Review > About Log Review

About Log Review

Log Review analyzes supplied or locally detected Veeam log sources and presents findings in a common review hierarchy. The same workflow can review a backup server, protected Agent host, application plug-in host, repository-side component, service evidence, or a mixed bundle containing several of those sources.

Common review model

SAT uses a product-neutral selection model wherever the evidence supports it:

System / Source
Machine, server, host, appliance, or other observed source
→
Product / Component
One or more product roles and components on that source
→
Job / Activity
Backup job, policy, plug-in operation, rescan, service activity, or other work item
→
Run
One observed execution or time-bounded occurrence

Not every Veeam product uses the same terms. SAT preserves product-specific names where they are useful and uses activity when the evidence does not describe a conventional backup job. See Product Context and Terminology.

Available review choices

ChoiceUse
Auto Detect Veeam Logs (Recommended)Normal starting point for single- or mixed-product evidence. SAT determines the applicable product/source profile from the supplied evidence.
Search Existing LogsDirect text search without building the full machine/product/activity/run review model.
Veeam Agent for Microsoft Windows overrideUse only when you intentionally want the Windows Agent parser for the selected source.
Veeam Backup & Replication overrideUse only when you intentionally want the VBR parser for the selected source.
Veeam Plug-In for Microsoft SQL Server overrideUse only for a known SQL Server plug-in source.
Veeam Plug-In for Oracle RMAN overrideUse only for a known RMAN plug-in source.
Generic ParserFor logs from several Veeam products, or from a product with no parser of its own: the parsing rules every Veeam log shares.

Auto Detect can identify evidence for Veeam Agent for Microsoft Windows, Veeam Agent for Linux, Veeam Agent for Mac, Veeam Agent for IBM AIX, Veeam Agent for Oracle Solaris, VBR, and supported plug-in/component sources. You do not need a separate manual review card for every product family.

Related topics

Adding Logs for ReviewUsing Auto DetectFast Index and Full ReviewEnvironment Review

Worker threads, CPU and how long a review takes

Log Review parses files in parallel. Left alone, SAT uses one worker per logical processor, capped at eight and never more than the number of files it found. The cap is deliberate: SAT is usually a guest on a machine that has other work to do.

Consider the host before raising it. On a backup server inside its backup window, on a proxy that is moving data, or on a repository under load, extra parser threads compete with the work the customer actually cares about. A slower review that finishes is better than a fast one that lands during a job. Core count is not the whole picture. On a machine with slow storage the review is bound by disk, and more workers will not help.

Every review reports what it used, so it can be measured: Workers Used, Elapsed and Throughput in lines per second are printed with the summary and written into the report. Run once, read those three numbers, and adjust only if they justify it.

SettingEffect
DefaultOne worker per logical processor, capped at eight and at the file count.
--workers NFixes the worker count. Clamped to at least one and never above the file count.
--single-threadOne worker. Use on a production host under load, or when isolating a parser problem.
Log Review > Product Context and Terminology

Product Context and Terminology

Multiple Products on One Machine

SAT can identify more than one Veeam product role on the same computer. A machine may, for example, run Veeam Backup & Replication, Veeam Agent for Microsoft Windows, a VSPC Management Agent, and an application plug-in at the same time. SAT keeps machine identity, product role, component, and management relationship separate.

Coexistence is not a management relationship. If VBR and an Agent are installed on the same machine, SAT records both roles. It only states that the local VBR manages that Agent when configuration or supplied evidence establishes the relationship. See Observed Relationships.
Evidence familyTypical sourceTypical activity terminologyPossible destination/context
Backup and replication platformBackup server or infrastructure componentJob, task, session, rescan, restore, maintenance activityRepository, proxy, gateway, managed workload
Endpoint or server AgentProtected Windows, Linux, Mac, IBM AIX, or Oracle Solaris systemJob, policy, backup run, restore activityBackup server, repository, cloud/service target
Application plug-inDatabase or application hostBackup/restore activity, channel, application-native operationBackup server, repository, transport component
Service / infrastructure evidenceRepository, gateway, proxy, transport service, management service, worker/applianceService activity or component finding; may not belong to a runRelated source, management system, or destination

If evidence cannot safely be bound to a job/run, SAT keeps it visible in the broader machine or environment scope. See Reviewing All Machines and Reviewing Machine Activity.

Log Review > Adding Logs

Adding Logs for Review

You can review a ZIP bundle, a directory tree, individual log files, or locally detected product log roots on a customer/lab host. When a selected root contains several recognizable machine-level groups, Auto Detect can separate those groups and treat each as its own computer.

To add a supplied log bundle, do the following:
  1. Open Log Review.
  2. Select Auto Detect Veeam Logs (Recommended) unless you need a manual parser override.
  3. Add the ZIP bundle, directory, or individual source.
  4. If additional evidence belongs to the same case, use Review New Logs / Append to add the evidence to the case.
  5. Start the review.
To review locally installed product logs without a case, do the following:
  1. Run SAT on the customer or lab computer.
  2. Enable Customer / Lab Execution Host.
  3. Leave Active case set to No Case.
  4. Open Log Review > Auto Detect Veeam Logs. SAT fills in the log folders of the Veeam products it detects on this machine and starts a fast index of them. When no Veeam logs are found, the status line says so; choose Generic Parser to select a folder yourself.
  5. If the evidence you need is outside those folders, add it to Log bundles / folders and index again.
Result. SAT performs an ad-hoc local review without creating persistent case state.
Multi-source exports. A support bundle can contain logs for several machines, products, services, plug-ins, repositories, or infrastructure components. SAT preserves source ownership when it can establish it and combines the results into the broader review model.

Log Review > Auto Detect

Using Auto Detect

Auto Detect Veeam Logs is the recommended review option when a bundle may contain more than one Veeam product or when the exact source type is not known before review.

What Auto Detect does

  • Examines the supplied evidence for product-specific signatures and collection metadata.
  • Recognizes multiple product roles on one machine or bundle.
  • Separates strong machine-level groups in mixed roots when they can be identified safely.
  • Keeps related transport, repository, service, or plug-in evidence as supporting components/relationships without automatically changing the source owner's product identity.
  • On a customer/lab host, can resolve known local log roots from the Veeam products detected on that machine. See Adding Logs for Review.
Use Product Identification when a source looks wrong. A support bundle can contain references to related Veeam infrastructure. Product Identification should describe the selected source owner from the strongest evidence; one related service or transport log does not by itself make that other product the owner of the source.

Fast Index and Full Review

Log Review can first produce an indexed preliminary result so you can identify machines, jobs, activities, and high-value evidence without waiting for every discovered log to be parsed deeply.

StatusMeaningWhat to do

FULLY ANALYZED: FULL REVIEW COMPLETEThe current source set has completed the full review path.Use system/source, job/activity, run, findings, components, and source evidence for detailed review.

Reviewing All Machines

When no single machine is selected, the center pane becomes Environment Activity Summary. It provides a quick comparison of the structured activity found for each machine.

ColumnMeaning
MachineThe machine represented by the structured source.
Latest activityThe newest structured job/activity resolved for that machine.

The findings table remains useful for standalone service or background symptoms that are not confidently associated with a job run. Broad views are newest-first by default and can be sorted by supported column headers.

To find the most recent problem in a multi-machine bundle, do the following:
  1. Select All Machines.
  2. Review Environment Activity Summary.
  3. Compare Latest activity, Last failure, and Last success.

Reviewing Machine Activity

When one machine is selected and no single job is selected, the center pane becomes Machine Activity Timeline. This view lists the structured jobs and related activities found for that machine, newest first.

Machine and Product

The Machine and Product pane contains machine identity and product information such as hostname, IP addresses, operating system, detected product, product version, management information, and source provenance.

Log Review > Jobs, Activities, and Run History

Reviewing Jobs, Activities, and Run History

Select a job or related activity to isolate its history on the chosen machine. When a job is selected and the Run selector remains at all matching runs, the center pane becomes Run History.

To compare several runs of the same job, do the following:
  1. Select the machine.
  2. Select the job or related activity.
  3. Leave Run set to All matching runs.
  4. Review the run windows, status, and finding counts.
  5. Choose the run that matches the reported time or the failure you want to investigate.
Result. Selecting an exact run changes the center pane to the detailed Selected Job Run view.

Related Veeam documentation

Veeam Backup & Replication: Protection Groups ↗
Log Review > Reviewing an Exact Run

Reviewing an Exact Run

An exact run is the most detailed Log Review scope. SAT shows run-specific settings and evidence and preserves the event sequence needed to understand how the run progressed.

Selected Job Run

Depending on what the logs contain, the Selected Job Run pane can include the run window, result, job type or mode, backup mode, destination or repository information, retention, compression, storage optimization, encryption, VSS details, source backup mode, repository operation, task size, PEX transfer performance and evidence counts, control events, and previous successful-run comparison data.

PEX transfer performance

While data moves, Veeam emits PEX samples: per-volume transfer performance records. Each sample carries six busy percentages, three for the source leg and three for the target leg. The highest percentage in a sample is the bottleneck that sample reports, and the stage that was highest most often across the run appears as PEX bottleneck in the Selected Job Run pane.

StageAlso calledWhat the percentage measures
Source read busySourceThe agent machine reading from the source disk.
Source processing busyProxyThe agent machine processing the read data, compressing it and packaging it for the network upload.
Source write busyNetworkThe upload on the network being completed.
Target read busyThe target downloading from the network.
Target processing busyThe target re-assembling the transferred packets into blocks, and then into backup files.
Target write busyTargetThe target writing the backup to the destination.

The run note repeats each stage peak and mean, with how many samples that stage was highest in, above the raw PEX lines. The alias is the word used in a support conversation: “the bottleneck is the network” is the source write percentage. Three fields in a PEX record have no confirmed meaning and are reported only as raw evidence.

Causal ordering

Exact-run findings are not freely sortable. Runs are selected newest-first, but the evidence inside an exact run is kept in chronological order from the start of the run toward its completion. This prevents a later follow-on error from being displayed above the earlier symptom that preceded it.
To review a failed run, do the following:
  1. Select the exact failed run.
  2. Read the run window and result.
  3. Review the finding sequence from the beginning of the run toward the failure.
  4. Select the earliest meaningful symptom and inspect its source evidence.
  5. Continue through later warnings or errors to determine whether they are follow-on symptoms.
  6. Use Last Known Good comparison rows when SAT resolved a previous successful run for the same machine and job.
  7. Add the relevant run findings or supporting evidence to #note.

Related topics

Reviewing Source EvidenceAdding Findings to #noteSorting and Chronology
Log Review > Components with Findings

Components with Findings

Components with Findings is separate from Machine and Product. It summarizes the components associated with findings in the current scope.

ColumnMeaning
ComponentThe component or evidence category associated with the finding, such as a service, VSS, repository, DataMover, or RPC/gRPC-related context.
Errors / WarningsGrouped finding counts associated with the component in the current selection.
Last seenThe newest retained timestamp for the component's findings.
EvidenceRetained location and source-file coverage.
Do not treat the component name as the symptom. A component tells you where SAT saw the finding. Read the finding text to determine what happened.

Log Review > Reviewing Findings and Symptoms

Reviewing Findings and Symptoms

The Issue Summary groups repeated error and warning evidence so that one recurring symptom does not occupy thousands of separate rows.

How to read a finding

Severity
ERROR
Time
Aug 11, 2026 14:44:18 UTC
Finding
Connection to the remote service failed.
Component
Transport / gRPC context
Evidence
Retained source path, line, raw log text, and grouped occurrence information

In this example, the review target is the connection failure. The component is supporting context that helps identify where the symptom was reported. SAT should not turn the component name itself into the problem statement.

Repeated findings

A grouped finding can show the total number of occurrences in the bundle, the retained occurrences in the current filter, first/last observed time, source coverage, and a bounded list of source locations. This lets you understand repetition without losing the ability to open supporting evidence.

Related topics

Components with FindingsReviewing Source EvidenceAdding Findings to #note
Log Review > Source Evidence

Persisted Source Coverage

Source Coverage is saved with the case review model. Reopening a case can therefore show each reviewed source path together with its evidence role, file size/line coverage, scan or cache state, elapsed processing time, deferred/error state, and role-level candidate/scanned/deferred/byte totals without rescanning the raw source merely to populate the view.

Reviewing Source Evidence

Select a finding to view its retained evidence. Source-backed findings keep the source path, line information when available, timestamp, and original text needed to return to the log.

Open evidence at the source

Use the source context menu to open the source at the selected line in the default application where supported, or use the SAT Viewer as the built-in fallback.

Stack traces keep file order. SAT can sort broad findings by time, but it does not reverse the lines inside an individual error stack or source-context block. Those lines remain in their original log order.

File Browser

Veeam & Case File Browser

File Browser provides direct access to registered SAT case workspaces, standard Veeam locations, SAT-owned locations and supported archives, with a console for commands on this machine. Remote machines are reached from Remote (SSH). The Local file view presents files and folders in a sortable details list so you can browse evidence before opening it in Log Review or adding it to a collection.

Pane / areaPurpose
Left navigation treeShows standard Veeam data/program locations, SAT-tracked case workspaces using their registered paths, and SAT-owned locations such as application logs.
Right file listShows file/folder icons and the Name, Type, Size, and Date modified columns. Folders are grouped before files. Select a supported column heading to sort; select the active heading again to reverse the order.
Location controlsShow the current location and provide Go/Refresh navigation. Use the parent entry to move to the containing folder. Filter rows at the end of the row filters the list; see Filtering a results table.
Windows System ToolsIn Windows Customer/Lab mode, provides shortcuts to Services, Event Viewer, Computer Management, Device Manager, Disk Management, and Certificates.

Double-click a directory to open it in SAT. On Windows, double-clicking a supported local file can use the normal Windows file association. Context menus provide path-copy, open, collection, and related actions where available.

Case roots use the registered case path. File Browser lists the cases SAT currently tracks and opens each case from its actual workspace location.

File Browser tabs

TabUseImportant behavior
LocalBrowse approved Veeam, tracked-case, and SAT roots; preview supported log/text evidence; browse supported archives read-only; send evidence to Log Review; mark local files/directories for collection.SAT validates approved roots during typed-path, parent, tree, and resolved link/junction navigation.
ConsoleRuns commands on this machine through PowerShell or CMD in one session, so a folder change or a variable carries to the next command; choosing the other shell starts the next command in a new session. Stop ends the session and a command still running in it, such as ping -t. Customer/Lab mode also provides an explicit Administrator option. SAT's folder is on the session's PATH and sat runs SAT, so a command copied from this guide runs as written, for example sat --help. In a CMD session a line that starts with sat runs through PowerShell, which waits for SAT and shows what it prints, so it takes PowerShell quoting.Command text is not written to Recent Activity. Elevated execution uses the normal UAC consent flow.

Marking Additional Files for Collection

Right-click an approved local file or directory and choose Mark for collection. Marked items are included by Universal Log Collection beneath Additional/Local/ with source-path/provenance information retained in the bundle manifest. Use Unmark to remove an item before collection. Remote files must first be explicitly downloaded into an approved local location.

Logs and Archives

Supported ZIP, 7z, and tar-family archives can be browsed read-only. SAT validates archive member paths before presenting content. Supported text/log evidence can be previewed with bounded output and sent to Log Review without requiring a general-purpose extraction workflow.

To browse files, do the following:
  1. Choose Go > File Browser.
  2. Select a location in the tree on the left: a standard Veeam location, a case workspace or a SAT-owned location.
  3. Select a column heading to sort the list, and select it again to reverse the order. Type in Filter rows to keep only the rows that contain the text.
  4. Double-click a folder to open it, or the parent entry to return to the containing folder.
To run a command on this machine from File Browser, do the following:
  1. Open the Console beside the file list.
  2. Choose PowerShell or Command Prompt (CMD) in Shell.
  3. Type the command and press Enter. sat in the Console runs this copy of SAT.
  4. Choose Stop to end the session and any command still running in it.

Log ReviewUniversal Log CollectionCase DashboardRemote File and Console Tools
Remote (SSH)

Remote (SSH)

Remote (SSH) opens an interactive shell on another machine beside a file pane for the same machine. Most of the machines in a Veeam case are not the one you are sitting at: the repository, the proxy, the database server running a plug-in. You connect, look, and pull only what you need, without asking the customer to zip a folder and send it.

Use it for Linux repositories, hardened repositories, Linux proxies, and any database server running a Veeam plug-in on Linux or Unix.

Connecting

  1. Enter the host, or pick a saved address from the Host list, and the port. Addresses are saved in Settings > SSH Addresses.
  2. Enter the user and either a password, or a private key file in the Key row below. Browse picks the file, and a key protected by a passphrase takes the passphrase in the field beside it.
  3. Choose Connect. SAT reads the host key and shows its SHA-256 fingerprint before any credential is sent. Compare it with the one from the server administrator, then choose Yes to trust it for this session.

The shell opens in the terminal. Tab is passed to the remote shell for completion. Select with the mouse, then Ctrl+Shift+C copies and Ctrl+Shift+V or Shift+Insert pastes; Ctrl+C remains the interrupt key.

The file pane

The file pane lists the folder in its path box, /var/log/VeeamBackup when a session opens, with the Size and Modified date of each file. Type another path and press Enter to list it. A folder that is not on the host opens the nearest folder above it, and the status line says so. [..] up one level goes to the containing folder, and a double-click opens a folder or downloads a file.

Download saves the selected file, and with a case open the save window starts in the case's logs folder. Upload sends a local file to the folder in the path box, keeping its name, and asks before it replaces a file of the same name there. Both run in the background: the status line counts the bytes as the file moves, and the window keeps responding. An upload lists the folder again when it finishes. A download is written to a temporary file and renamed only when complete, so an interrupted transfer does not leave half a log behind.

Hosts that refuse SFTP still work. A hardened Veeam repository commonly disables the SFTP subsystem while leaving an interactive shell available. When SAT cannot open SFTP it falls back to listing the directory over the shell, and transfers fall back to SCP. If a host refuses both, the status line gives the reason the host returned, so you can tell a refused connection from a rejected account.
Credentials are session-only. The password and the key's passphrase are held for the life of the session only. They are not saved into the case, are not written to the activity log, and are not included in a collection. Disconnect closes the session and clears both.
Path scope. The approved-root restriction described in Veeam & Case File Browser applies to the File Browser browse tree only. The Remote (SSH) file pane opens any folder the signed-in account can read.

Drag the divider between the file pane and the terminal to give either one more room; see Resizing and collapsing panes.

To connect to a remote machine and pull a file, do the following:
  1. Choose Go > Remote (SSH).
  2. Type the host, or pick a saved address from the Host list, and the port.
  3. Type the user and either a password or a private key file. Choose Browse to pick the key file, and type the passphrase in the field beside it if the key has one.
  4. Choose Connect. Compare the SHA-256 fingerprint shown with the one from the server administrator, then choose Yes to trust it for this session.
  5. Type a path in the box above the file pane and press Enter to list it.
  6. Select a file and choose Download. With a case open, the save window starts in the case's logs folder.
  7. Choose Disconnect to end the session. The passphrase is cleared.

Remote File and Console Tools

Use Remote (SSH) to move a specific file between this machine and a connected host, and the File Browser Console tab for a bounded command session on this machine.

SSH file transfer

To connect and transfer a file, do the following:
  1. Open Remote (SSH).
  2. Enter the host, port, user, and a password, or a private key file with its passphrase when it has one.
  3. Choose Connect, compare the SHA-256 fingerprint SAT shows with the one from the server administrator, and trust it for this session.

Console

The Console tab of File Browser runs commands on this machine through PowerShell or CMD. The session stays open between commands, so a folder change carries to the next one, and Stop ends it along with a command that is still running. Customer/Lab mode also provides an explicit Administrator option. SAT's folder is on the session's PATH and sat runs SAT.

Command responsibility. The console runs the commands you enter with the permissions of the session. Review the elevation state before running a command. Recent Activity records the run and not the command text.

Environment Review > About Environment Review

About Environment Review

Environment Review uses one dashboard with three evidence sources: live Customer/Lab machine state, a read-only imported environment.log, or the active Engineer case parser model. A count on a card is a starting point for inspection. Cards stream independently. Below them, the topology is on the left, the selected node's detail on the right, and the report across the bottom, with a draggable divider between each; see Resizing and collapsing panes. A tabular section opens as a grid. A wide section or report scrolls sideways, so its columns stay aligned.

  • Customer/Lab (Windows): no case is required. Eight cards stream independently for System, Veeam Products, Windows Maintenance, Services, Installed Software, Network, TLS / Security, and Veeam Certificates / Registry. Left-click opens detail. Right-click provides Open details, Copy summary, and Copy all details. The page keeps the collection: opening it again shows the same cards, and the subtitle gives the time the collection completed. Refresh live machine collects again.
  • Imported snapshot: Engineer Review loads collected SAT_ENVIRONMENT_V2 snapshots read-only and remains compatible with older SAT_ENVIRONMENT_V1 snapshots.
  • Active case: SAT renders parser-derived systems, roles, source ownership and observed protection flows. Case metrics are also interactive cards; the complete evidence-backed report remains available for PDF/copy workflows. The case model is read again only when a review changes it, when you switch case, or on Refresh case topology.
Counts are drillable. For example, a Services or Installed Software card can be opened to see the itemized alphabetical inventory as well as a running/total count.
The parser result is what the report is built from. Product documentation defines valid workflow shapes; SAT shows a concrete relationship only when the supplied evidence supports it.

Quick checks and section grids

A section of the collection that holds rows, such as Adapters, Routes or TLS Cipher Suite Order, shows in the details pane as a grid, each column as wide as its values and the grid scrolling sideways when needed. A field of name=value pairs gets a column per name.

Quick checks in the tree lists the newest Name Check, Time Check, Local Port Checker and Volume Check run on each machine, with its outcome; choose one for its rows. On Customer / Lab these are this machine's runs, and a new run joins the tree without collecting again. In Engineer Review they come from the active case's logs, as each imported collection carries them.

To review the environment, do the following:
  1. Choose Go > Environment Review. In Customer / Lab the cards for this machine fill in as each collection finishes. In Engineer Review the page shows the active case.
  2. Click a card to open its detail, or right-click it for Open details, Copy summary and Copy all details.
  3. Select a node in the topology to read its detail on the right, and the report along the bottom.
  4. Type in Filter rows to narrow a table section.
  5. In Customer / Lab, choose Refresh live machine to collect again. In Engineer Review, use Open to load a collected environment snapshot.

Related topics

Systems and ProductsObserved RelationshipsObserved Protection FlowSystem and Health Context
Environment Review > Systems and Products

Systems and Products

The case dashboard groups source owners, protected workloads/application hosts, management/control systems, repositories/targets and other observed components, not every run as another top-level relationship. Hostnames, IP addresses, product/version and management evidence remain attached to the owning machine when available.

The live/imported dashboard uses the same visual surface for operating-system and machine inventory so the customer snapshot can be reviewed later on an engineer workstation.

Windows Environment cardExamples of detail
SystemWindows product/version/build/architecture, boot/install context, manufacturer/model, system UUID, BIOS, CPU/memory and SAT elevation state.
Windows MaintenanceIdentified CBS/QFE hotfix evidence plus installed Windows servicing-package evidence and available installation metadata. QFE collection can remain available without elevation; when the servicing-package stage requires administrator rights, SAT requests UAC approval and continues to show the already-collected QFE evidence if approval is declined or the elevated package query is unavailable.
Services / Installed SoftwareItemized service name/display name/state/start mode/account/PID and registry-backed installed application/version/publisher/location inventory.
NetworkAdapters, link/driver context, IPv4/IPv6 interface state, MTU, metrics, DHCP, DNS/gateway, routes and advanced adapter properties such as vendor-exposed jumbo-frame values.
TLS / SecuritySCHANNEL protocol overrides, OS-default/explicit state context, ordered cipher suites and firewall profiles. SAT observes; it does not change TLS policy.
Veeam Certificates / RegistryPublic metadata for Veeam-named LocalMachine certificates and read-only HKLM\SOFTWARE\Veeam inventory with secret-like values redacted. Private keys are not exported.
Shared log paths are not product identity. Paths such as C:\ProgramData\Veeam\Backup, /var/log/VeeamBackup and /var/log/veeam may contain evidence from several Veeam components. Product-only tools require a real installation/service/package capability signature.

Environment Review presents relationships graphically/compactly by evidence role: management/control, protected workload or plug-in host, product-specific transport/worker/data mover, and repository/target. SAT uses product-specific workflow knowledge to interpret logs without turning documentation into case facts. Health Monitor > About Health Monitor

About Health Monitor

Health Monitor provides a point-in-time view of resource pressure and system activity. The exact telemetry depends on the current operating system and what the hardware/OS exposes.

AreaExamples
CPUUtilization and available temperature/thermal information.
MemoryPhysical memory, committed/virtual memory, swap/paging and page activity where exposed.
StorageFilesystem capacity and available device state/latency/health information.
NetworkPer-interface receive/transmit counters, errors/drops, link state, and speed where exposed.
ProcessesTop processes/threads and resource/I/O information where supported.

Windows provides the broadest Windows-specific device/service integration. Linux uses native /proc, /sys, filesystem, and network interfaces. macOS uses native Mach, sysctl, libproc, filesystem, and network APIs. If a sensor or metric is unavailable, SAT reports it as unavailable.

Use Live Health on a Customer/Lab host and Saved Health Snapshot on the engineer workstation. The current health snapshot can also be included in Universal Log Collection system context.

Health Monitor > Live Health

Using Live Health Monitor

Live sampling is available only while SAT is in Customer / Lab Execution Host mode.

To review live system health, do the following:
  1. On the system being examined, enable Customer / Lab Tools (this session).
  2. Open Health Monitor.
  3. Wait for the first sample to populate.
  4. Review the summary cards and active findings.
  5. Left-click a card to open its detailed view.
  6. Review CPU/temperature, memory, paging, storage, network, and process details as needed.
Point-in-time view. Health Monitor is intended for quick triage. A saved snapshot represents the state captured at that time and is not presented as current live telemetry later.

Live, these are this machine's runs; with a saved snapshot open in Engineer Review, the active case's runs on that snapshot's machine.
