Tools > Host Diagnostics > Host Checks

Host Checks

Host Checks reads what most often explains a failed snapshot or backup on this machine and lists it as a table of Group, Check, Detail and Status. It changes nothing and starts no program. Open Tools > Host Diagnostics in the Customer / Lab role and choose Host Checks. Tick the checks to run, set Days for the events, then choose Run checks.

Before you start

  • To read VSS shadow storage, start SAT as administrator first. The other checks run as a standard user.
CheckWhat it reads
Backup eventsvolsnap 25 and 36, VSS 8193 and 12289, disk 129 and 153, and NTFS 55 and 98 in the System and Application logs over Days: how many, the first and the newest, and the newest event's own text, as an event id alone does not name the cause.
Veeam driversEvery driver whose name starts with Veeam, with its state, how it starts and its file, and the change tracking store in C:\ProgramData\Veeam\CtpStore.
VSS shadow storageEach volume's used, allocated and maximum shadow storage, where it is kept, and its shadow copies. Used at the maximum is a Finding: Windows deletes older shadow copies, and a new one can be aborted. Needs administrator.
.NET and TLSThe .NET Framework release, SchUseStrongCrypto and SystemDefaultTlsVersions in the 64-bit and 32-bit views, and the SCHANNEL Enabled and DisabledByDefault values of each TLS version. An absent value is the Windows default. TLS 1.2 turned off is a Finding.

Finding is something the logs or settings show; Information is what is there; Not present means the item does not exist on this machine. The checks, events and names are a data file in SAT, so a new Veeam release changes data, not the program.

The command-line twin is system host-checks, for example SupportAssistTool.exe system host-checks --checks events,shadow-storage --days 30; it exits 3 on a finding.

To run the host checks, do the following:
  1. Open Tools > Host Diagnostics in the Customer / Lab role and choose Host Checks.
  2. Tick the checks to run. Each group is a tick box.
  3. In Days, set how many days of events to read. The default is 7.
  4. Choose Run checks. The table lists each check with its group, detail and status.
  5. Select a row to read its whole text in the pane under the table.
FieldWhat it does
DaysOptional. How many days of System and Application events the Backup events check reads. Empty reads 7 days.
Backup eventsOptional. Reads the System and Application events that explain failed snapshots and storage trouble: volsnap, VSS, disk and NTFS. Ticked to begin with.
Veeam driversOptional. Lists the Veeam drivers on this machine with their state and how each starts, and the change tracking store. Ticked to begin with.
VSS shadow storage (administrator)Optional. Reads the shadow storage of each volume: used, allocated and maximum space, and the shadow copies on it. Needs administrator rights. Ticked to begin with.
.NET and TLSOptional. Reads the .NET Framework release and the registry values that turn TLS 1.2 on or off. Ticked to begin with.

Tools > Host Diagnostics > Named Pipes

Named Pipes

Veeam components on one machine talk to each other over named pipes: Veeam Agent for Microsoft Windows' service channel, the mount server API and the satellite processes of a backup server, and SQL Server's own endpoints. Named Pipes lists every pipe in \\.\pipe\ on this machine by name, with how many instances each has, and marks the pipes of Veeam products, SQL Server and PostgreSQL with their purpose and service. Use it when a Veeam service reports that it cannot reach another one on the same machine. Open it from Tools > Host Diagnostics, under HOST CHECKS, in the Customer / Lab role.

To list the named pipes, do the following:
  1. In Customer / Lab, open Tools > Host Diagnostics and choose Named Pipes.
  2. Fill in the fields. The table below describes each.
  3. Choose List pipes.

Before You Begin

Named Pipes reads the list of pipe names only. It opens no pipe and waits on none, so a pipe that takes one client at a time is left free. It needs no administrator.

Listing the pipes

To list the pipes, do the following:

  1. Open Tools > Host Diagnostics and click Named Pipes.
  2. In Pipes shown, choose Every pipe or Veeam pipes.
  3. Click List pipes.
  4. Type in Filter rows to narrow the table, and click a row to read it in full below the table.
FieldWhat it does
Pipes shownEvery pipe lists the whole pipe namespace. Veeam pipes keeps the pipes of Veeam products, SQL Server and PostgreSQL, and the pipes of Veeam programs.

What the results mean

ColumnWhat it shows
PipeThe pipe's name after \\.\pipe\.
InstancesHow many instances the pipe has, and how many it allows: 18 of unlimited, 1 of 1. A pipe at its maximum takes no new client until one disconnects.
Known asThe product and purpose of a pipe SAT knows, such as Veeam Agent for Microsoft Windows: Service channel (gRPC) of the Agent's service. Empty for any other pipe.
Service or processThe service that holds a known pipe, with its state and process ID, such as VeeamMountSvc, running, PID 10752. A pipe whose name carries a process ID, such as the .NET diagnostics port dotnet-diagnostic-716, shows that process and the service it runs. not installed means the service is not on this machine.

The result line counts the pipes listed, the Veeam or database pipes and the pipes named by their process. The pipe names SAT knows are a data file in SAT. Environment Review shows the Veeam pipes as a Named Pipes section of its Services card, and a log collection keeps them in its environment snapshot.

The command-line twin is system pipes, for example SupportAssistTool.exe system pipes --veeam.

Host DiagnosticsInstaller Cache CheckCommand-Line Reference
Tools > Host Diagnostics > Installer Cache Check

Installer Cache Check

Windows keeps a copy of each installed product's .msi, and of each patch's .msp, in C:\Windows\Installer. When that copy has been deleted, uninstalling, repairing or upgrading the product asks for the original installer, and Programs and Features can list the product without its version. Installer Cache Check lists what Windows Installer records of each product, says whether its cached package is still there, and checks an installer you have against them. The check only reads. Open it from Tools > Host Diagnostics, under INSTALLED SOFTWARE, in the Customer / Lab role.

FieldWhat to enter
UpgradeCode or product namePart of a product's name or publisher, or an UpgradeCode with or without braces. Veeam, the default, lists every product Veeam installed; an empty field lists every installed product. A ProductCode entered here lists the product it names.
Installer, or a folder, to check (optional)An .msi, an .exe, or a folder such as a mounted ISO. Browse offers an installer or a folder.

The results are a table of Product, Item, Value and State. The rows are grouped by product: a row with the product's name, then its items under it, one row for each item:

ItemWhat it shows
Installer cache folderC:\Windows\Installer and how many .msi and .msp files it holds.
ProductCode, UpgradeCode, Version, Installed onThe product's identity as Windows Installer records it. The UpgradeCode is shared by every version of a product line.
Programs and FeaturesThe name and version of the product's own Uninstall entry, which is what Programs and Features lists, beside the Version that Windows Installer records: SAME VERSION or DIFFERENT VERSION.
Original packageThe file name of the .msi the product was installed from.
PackageCodeThe identity of that exact package. Windows takes an installer as the product's source only when its PackageCode is this one.
Last used sourceThe folder or media the product was last installed from.
Cached packageThe copy Windows expects in C:\Windows\Installer: PRESENT, or MISSING when it has been deleted.
PatchEach patch applied to the product, with its cached .msp, PRESENT or MISSING.
Main programThe program the product's Uninstall entry names, or else the largest program in its install folder whose version information names the product, with its file version: SAME VERSION when it is the product's version.
Read from the registryThe values Windows Installer returned nothing for, read from its registry keys instead.

Checking an installer

  • An .msi shows its PackageCode, ProductCode, UpgradeCode and version. Match reads MATCH when its PackageCode is a listed product's: it is the package that product was installed from, the one Windows asks for. DIFFERENT BUILD means it shares only the ProductCode or the UpgradeCode: the same product in another build or version. An Installed row says whether a product with its ProductCode or UpgradeCode is installed and at which version, against the package's: SAME VERSION, DIFFERENT VERSION or NOT INSTALLED.
  • An .exe shows its file version, its signer and whether a listed product has its version. An .exe installer carries its .msi packages inside it, so check those .msi files, such as the ones on the product's ISO.
  • A folder is searched four levels down for .msi files, and each is read as an .msi, the one that matches first.

Every file checked shows its SHA-256. A product the installer relates to by its UpgradeCode or ProductCode is listed too, whatever the field holds. When a Cached package reads MISSING, the installer Windows asks for is the one whose PackageCode matches; Original package gives its file name.

The command-line twin is system installer-cache, for example SupportAssistTool.exe system installer-cache --name Veeam --check D:\; it exits 3 when a cached package is missing.

To check the installed Veeam products, do the following:
  1. Open Tools > Host Diagnostics in the Customer / Lab role and choose Installer Cache Check.
  2. Leave UpgradeCode or product name at Veeam to list the products Veeam installed, or type part of another product's name, an UpgradeCode or a ProductCode.
  3. To check an installer, choose Browse beside Installer, or a folder, to check (optional) and pick an .msi, an .exe or a folder such as a mounted ISO.
  4. Choose Check. The table lists each product with its items and their state.
  5. Select a row to read its whole text in the pane under the table.

The Windows Installer API supplies each product's details. The Installer registry keys fill a value the API leaves empty, and give a product's UpgradeCode, which the API does not return.

Diagnostics

Diagnostics is a separate application area for SAT and system diagnostic views. Nothing here opens a tool tab or counts against the tool session limit. It shows System Information, Products and Integrations, the SAT Self-Test and the Requirements as one report, read when the page opens. Run again reads them again, and Copy gives the report as text. AreaPurpose
System InformationReview machine identity, join state, firmware, operating-system, and related system information using the platform-appropriate native sources.
Products and IntegrationsReview detected Veeam product/integration presence and supporting context.

Requirements

The Requirements section follows the SAT Self-Test. It lists what the Windows tools use and whether each is present: .NET, Windows PowerShell and PowerShell 7, the execution policy, the Windows build, the service manager, the WMI service, administrator rights, the SQL Server ODBC drivers and psql.

Application Reference > Recent Activity

Recent Activity

Recent Activity is the history of what SAT has run on this machine, newest first: when each run or action took place, what it was, and how it ended. It is recorded with or without an engineer licence, in either role, with or without a case.

TileLists
ALL ENTRIESEverything recorded, newest first
FINDINGSChecks that reported something to review
FAILEDRuns and actions that ended with an error
CANCELLEDStopped on request before completing

Choose a tile to list only those entries; choose it again for all of them. The Result column says how each ended in a few words, such as Completed, passed or Completed, with findings; the full outcome is in Details. The page shows the newest 500 entries.

A Customer / Lab collection carries the history in its bundle. In Engineer Review, open a collected record (its activity TSV, the collection folder or its archive) to read it in place of this machine's; Show live activity returns to this machine's own history.

To read the activity on this machine, do the following:
  1. Choose Recent Activity in the rail or in Go > Recent Activity. The newest 500 entries are listed.
  2. Choose a tile to list only the entries of that kind. Choose the tile again to list all entries.
  3. Select an entry to read its details.
To read a collected activity record, do the following:
  1. In Engineer Review, choose Open Read-Only and choose the collected activity TSV, the collection folder or its archive.
  2. Read the entries. They are shown in place of this machine's history.
  3. Choose Show live activity to return to this machine's own history.

Quick ToolsDiagnostics
Integrations

Integrations

Integrations is a grouped catalogue of the optional utilities SAT can work with. SAT looks for each tool in the usual places: PATH, the registry and the standard program folders. A tool found there is used in place. A tool not found is either not installed or a portable copy in a folder outside these places.

Tools are shown as cards in four groups:

GroupWhat is in it
Your ToolsPrograms you configured yourself (see Configured Tools).
LaunchPrograms that open their own window: Process Monitor and Wireshark.
AssistedTools SAT runs for you: Packet Monitor, ETL2PCAPNG, iPerf3 and DiskSpd in a Run window, and VSS Trace with Run and Stop.
DatabaseDatabase clients that open the database console: SQLCMD and psql (PostgreSQL).

Each card shows a status, so you can see at a glance what SAT found:

StatusMeaning
DetectedFound already installed on this machine; SAT uses it in place.
ManagedIn SAT's tools folder: a copy SAT downloaded, or one placed there by hand.
Built-inPart of Windows (for example Packet Monitor); nothing to acquire.
Not presentNot found. The card offers to acquire it, or to open the vendor page.
AvailableA tool of your own whose program is where you said.
MissingA tool of your own whose program is no longer there.

The buttons at the top of the page are Add tool, which adds a program of your own to Your Tools, Open tools folder and Refresh, which looks for the tools again after one is installed or placed by hand.

To use a tool from Integrations, do the following:
  1. Open Integrations from the rail or from Go > Integrations.
  2. Select the tool's card. Its detail opens on the right.
  3. Choose the action the detail offers: Acquire for a tool that is not present, Update for a downloaded copy, Launch for a windowed tool, or Run for a tool with a guided run.
  4. Choose File location to see where the tool is, Remove to delete a copy SAT downloaded, or Open tools folder to open the tools folder.
Integrations > Acquiring a tool

Acquiring a tool

Acquire downloads a tool over HTTPS from the link built into this SAT, and the download is checked before anything from it reaches the tools folder:

  • An installer (Wireshark's MSI) must be signed by the publisher SAT expects before it is unpacked or run. The command that unpacks it is fixed in SAT.
  • An archive's programs must each be signed by the expected publisher: Microsoft for DiskSpd, etl2pcapng, Process Monitor, sqlcmd and VSS Trace. iPerf3's and psql's publishers sign nothing, so each download must match the SHA-256 this SAT expects. A download that fails its check is removed, and the result names the file and the signer found.

The links and publishers are part of the SAT build; a new link comes with a new SAT. Update replaces a downloaded copy and removes the earlier versions SAT installed. A windowed tool such as Wireshark or Process Monitor shows Launch once it is present. Process Monitor also has Start capture and Stop capture; see Process Monitor.

Without an engineer licence SAT downloads nothing: Acquire and Update name the tool's official page and the folder to place it in, with Copy path, Open folder and Open official page.

To acquire a tool, do the following:
  1. Open Integrations and select the tool's card.
  2. Choose Acquire. SAT downloads the tool over HTTPS and checks it before it reaches the tools folder.
  3. Choose Launch or Run when the card shows the tool as Managed.
  4. To replace a downloaded copy with the latest one, choose Update.
To place a tool by hand without a licence, do the following:
  1. Select the tool's card and choose Acquire. SAT shows the tool's official page and the folder to place it in.
  2. Choose Open official page, download the tool, and put it in the folder named. Copy path and Open folder help with the folder.

Related topics

About IntegrationsGuided runsDisk Speed Test
Integrations > Guided runs

Guided runs

A guided run opens a window with a form for a tool, its live output, and the command line it ran. Packet Monitor, ETL2PCAPNG, iPerf3 and DiskSpd (the Disk Speed Test) each have one, so a run needs no command written by hand. The run is logged to the active case, or to Log-Collections when no case is active.

Before You Begin

  • Acquire the tool on Integrations first. See Acquiring a tool.
  • For iPerf3, start the server on one machine and the client on the other. Both use the same port, 5201 by default, and a firewall between them must let it through.

The window has a Preset list, the fields of the tool, a Full output pane, and the buttons Run, CLI and Close. A field with a fixed set of choices is a drop-down. Every field has hover text, and Tab moves between the fields. CLI shows the SAT command and the tool's own command line for the form.

Related topics

IntegrationsAcquiring a toolNetwork ThroughputDisk Speed Test
Integrations > Guided runs > iPerf3 throughput

iPerf3 throughput

The iPerf3 Run window measures network throughput between this machine and another machine that runs iPerf3, such as a proxy and its repository.

FieldWhat it does
ModeClient sends to the other machine's iPerf3 server and measures. Server waits for a client; start it first, on the other machine.
ServerThe machine running the iPerf3 server, by name or address, such as the repository.
DirectionUpload: this machine sends to the server, as a proxy writes to a repository. Download: the server sends to this machine, as a restore does.
StreamsSingle uses one connection. Multiple uses several at once, as Veeam's data movers do. A much higher result with several streams points at a limit on each connection.
Number of streamsHow many connections at once when Streams is Multiple. The default is 5, the number of upload streams Veeam uses for a job by default.
Duration (seconds)How long the client sends. The default is 20; 60 gives a steadier figure.
PortThe server's port, 5201 by default. Both machines use the same port.
ProtocolTCP measures what a connection achieves, as Veeam's traffic does. UDP sends at a set rate to show lost packets and jitter.
PresetWhat it sets
Quick check: one stream for 20 secondsOne connection to the server for 20 seconds. Start the Server preset on the other machine first.
Veeam default: five streams for a minuteFive connections at once for a minute, uploading. Compare it with one stream.
Like a restore: five streams back to this machineThe server sends to this machine for a minute on five connections, as data flows in a restore.
Server: wait for the other machineThis machine waits on port 5201 for the client to connect. Press Stop when done.
To measure throughput between two machines with iPerf3, do the following:
  1. On the machine that receives, open Integrations, select iPerf3 and choose Run.
  2. In Preset, choose Server: wait for the other machine, then choose Run. The server waits for the client.
  3. On the other machine, open the iPerf3 Run window. In Preset, choose Veeam default: five streams for a minute, or Like a restore: five streams back to this machine to measure the other direction.
  4. Type the first machine's name or address in Server and choose Run.
  5. Read the throughput in the output. Choose CLI to see the command that ran.
  6. On the first machine, stop the server and choose Close.

Related topics

Guided runs
Integrations > Removing a downloaded copy

Removing a downloaded copy

If SAT downloaded and manages a local copy of a tool, Remove copy deletes that SAT-owned copy from the tools folder. It does not uninstall a program you installed yourself or one installed through the operating system.

To remove a downloaded copy, do the following:
  1. Open Integrations and select the card of a tool that shows Managed.
  2. Choose Remove copy. The copy SAT downloaded is deleted from the tools folder.

Related topics

DiagnosticsNetwork ThroughputSQL ToolsPrivacy and Collection Boundaries
Integrations > Your Tools > Configured Tools

Configured Tools

SAT can launch a program you already trust and point it at the evidence you have open. SAT launches only the programs you configure by hand.

The four actions are on Integrations:

ActionWhat it does
Configured ToolsLists what is configured on this copy of SAT.
Add a Configured ToolGive the entry a name, the full path to the program, and the argument line to run it with.
Run a Configured ToolRuns the entry against the case and evidence currently open.
Remove a Configured ToolRemoves the entry. The program itself is left alone.

Three placeholders in the argument line are replaced when the tool runs, so a second parser can be pointed at the same bundle without navigating it there by hand:

PlaceholderBecomes
{case}The active case folder.
{evidence}The active case's logs folder.
{selected}The file selected in File Browser.

A placeholder with nothing behind it stops the launch and reports the empty field.

Privileges. A configured tool runs at the privilege level of SAT and is not elevated. Give the program as a full path. The arguments go to the program directly, not through a shell.

To add and run a configured tool, do the following:
  1. Open Integrations and choose Add tool in Your Tools.
  2. Type a Name, the full path of the program in Executable, and the Arguments. Use {case}, {evidence} and {selected} where the tool needs the open case, its logs or the file selected in File Browser.
  3. Choose Save Tool. The tool appears in Your Tools.
  4. Select the tool and choose Run. The tool runs against the case and evidence currently open.
  5. To remove the entry, select it and choose Remove. The program itself is left alone.

Related topics

About Integrations
Integrations > Your Tools > Adding Your Own Tools

Adding Your Own Tools

SAT can launch another program you name, so a tool you always reach for is one click away inside the case you are working.

Open ApplicationLogs\configured-tools.tsv, which SAT writes when a tool is added with an engineer licence; it can also be created by hand. Each line is one tool, with tab-separated fields: an id, the name the button shows, the absolute path to the executable, its arguments, whether to start in the active case folder, and a note. The file itself lists the fields and carries a commented example to copy.

Three placeholders are substituted when the tool runs: {case} is the active case folder, {evidence} its evidence folder, and {selected} whatever you have selected. Only the entries in this file are offered, and a configured tool runs as the same account SAT is running as, without elevation.

To add your own tool, do the following:
  1. Open ApplicationLogs\configured-tools.tsv in a text editor.
  2. Add a line for the tool, with the fields tab-separated as the file's example shows.
  3. Save the file.
  4. On Integrations, choose Refresh.
Expected result. The tool shows under Your Tools with a Run button.

Related topics

About Integrations
Integrations > Launch > Process Monitor

Process Monitor

Process Monitor, from Microsoft Sysinternals, records process, registry and file activity live, so you can see what a Veeam process touches and where it is denied or blocked. Use it for permission, path and locking problems the logs only hint at.

Before You Begin

  • To get Process Monitor, choose Acquire on its card first. The download is checked against Microsoft's signature. See Acquiring a tool.
  • To capture, approve the Windows prompt: Process Monitor runs as administrator, so when SAT does not, Windows asks at Start capture and again at Stop capture.

Launch opens Process Monitor's own window, where a filter is set and a capture is opened. Start capture runs it in the background with the filter it last saved, or a .pmc filter file you choose, and writes a .pml capture to Tools\procmon in Log-Collections, or to the active case's logs in Engineer Review. Stop capture ends it, and closing SAT ends it too.

To capture with Process Monitor, do the following:
  1. Open Integrations and select the Process Monitor card.
  2. Choose Start capture. When SAT is not running as administrator, approve the Windows prompt.
  3. Reproduce the problem.
  4. Choose Stop capture and approve the prompt again.
  5. To read the capture, choose Launch and open the .pml file in Process Monitor.
Expected result. The .pml capture is in Tools\procmon under Log-Collections, or in the active case's logs.

Related topics

About IntegrationsAcquiring a toolHost Diagnostics
Integrations > Launch > Wireshark

Wireshark

Wireshark is the interactive protocol analyzer. Open a PCAPNG capture in it to inspect packets, follow conversations and filter by host or protocol, when a capture needs more than a count of events.

Before You Begin

  • To get Wireshark, choose Acquire on its card first. SAT downloads the stable release's installer, checks that the Wireshark Foundation signed it, and unpacks it into the tools folder without installing it. See Acquiring a tool.
  • To capture live in Wireshark, install Npcap first, separately and with administrator rights. Opening a capture file needs nothing more.
To open a capture in Wireshark, do the following:
  1. Capture with Packet Monitor or Packet Capture on Network Tools, or convert an .etl capture with ETL2PCAPNG.
  2. Open Integrations, select the Wireshark card and choose Launch.
  3. In Wireshark, open the .pcapng file from the File menu.

Related topics

About IntegrationsPacket MonitorPacket Capture
Integrations > Assisted > Packet Monitor

Packet Monitor

Packet Monitor (pktmon) is Windows' own packet capture, so it is Built-in and there is nothing to acquire. Its Run window captures the traffic of the host and port that fail, then converts the capture to .pcapng for Wireshark. Network Tools' Packet Capture uses it too.

Before You Begin

  • To capture, approve the Windows prompt: the capture runs as administrator.
FieldWhat it does
HostOnly traffic to or from this machine: the agent, the repository or the gateway. Empty captures every host.
PortOnly traffic on this port: 445 for SMB (agent deployment, file shares), 443 for HTTPS (object storage). Empty captures every port.
CaptureHeaders keeps the start of each packet, enough to follow connections. Full packets keeps everything for a closer look in Wireshark, and the capture grows faster.
PresetWhat it sets
SMB: agent deployment and file shares (port 445)Traffic on port 445. Put the target machine in Host to keep the capture small.
HTTPS: object storage (port 443)Traffic on port 443, as object storage and other HTTPS services use.
Everything to and from one hostEvery port, for the machine named in Host.
To capture with Packet Monitor, do the following:
  1. Open Integrations, select the Packet Monitor card and choose Run.
  2. Choose a preset, or fill Host, Port and Capture.
  3. Choose Run and approve the Windows prompt.
  4. Reproduce the problem, then choose Stop.
Expected result. The capture is converted to .pcapng and saved under Log-Collections, ready for Wireshark.

Related topics

Guided runsWiresharkPacket Capture
Integrations > Assisted > ETL2PCAPNG

ETL2PCAPNG

ETL2PCAPNG, from Microsoft, converts an .etl network capture into a .pcapng that Wireshark can open. Use it for a capture Packet Monitor's own converter cannot read.

Before You Begin

  • To get ETL2PCAPNG, choose Acquire on its card first. The download is checked against Microsoft's signature.
FieldWhat it does
Capture (.etl)The capture to convert: PktMon.etl from Packet Monitor, or another .etl network capture.
Save as (.pcapng)Where to write the converted capture. Empty writes it beside the active case's logs, or in Log-Collections with no case active.
To convert a capture, do the following:
  1. Open Integrations, select the ETL2PCAPNG card and choose Run.
  2. In Capture (.etl), choose the .etl file.
  3. Leave Save as (.pcapng) empty, or choose where to write the result.
  4. Choose Run.
Expected result. The .pcapng is written, ready to open in Wireshark.

Related topics

Packet MonitorWiresharkGuided runs
Integrations > Assisted > VSS Trace

VSS Trace

VSS Trace records a detailed trace of Windows' shadow copy service while a backup fails, as Veeam's KB3164 describes. Use it for VSS writer and snapshot failures the event log does not explain.

Before You Begin

  • To get VSS Trace, choose Acquire on its card first. SAT downloads the archive KB3164 names and checks Microsoft's signature on its programs.
  • To trace, approve the Windows prompt: VSS Trace runs as administrator.

Run starts VSS Trace with the flags KB3164 gives (+f 0xffff -l 255) and writes the trace to <host>_vsstrace.log in the vsstrace folder of this machine's tool output, under Log-Collections. A question shows the file before it starts.

To trace a VSS failure, do the following:
  1. Open Integrations, select the VSS Trace card and choose Run.
  2. Choose OK on the question that names the trace file, and approve the Windows prompt.
  3. Reproduce the failing backup.
  4. Choose Stop.
Expected result. The trace is in the vsstrace folder under Log-Collections, and Log Collection takes it with the rest of the tool output.

Related topics

VSS ToolsSnapshot (VSS) fails during backupAbout Integrations
Integrations > Assisted > Disk Speed Test

Disk Speed Test

The Disk Speed Test measures how fast storage reads and writes, with DiskSpd as its engine: the tests Veeam's KB2014 gives for a repository (active full, merge, reverse incremental, restore) and a source, and a test of your own. It is an integration: acquire DiskSpd on Integrations, then press its Run.

  • Test. Pick a preset, or set your own mix of reads and writes, block size, threads and duration.
  • Where. A write test writes only SAT's own new test file in the folder chosen and removes it afterwards; a read test opens an existing file for reading only.
  • Used as. Say whether the storage is a backup repository, the source a backup reads, or other, so the result says what it means for that role.
  • Result. Simple first: reads and writes apart, in MB/s and GB/s, what SAT did and what it means, then the full results. The run is kept as result.json, which the File Transfer Calculator can open as the storage speed.

SAT checks Microsoft's signature on diskspd.exe before each run.

Before You Begin

  • Acquire DiskSpd on Integrations. See Acquiring a tool.
  • On a backup server, run the test when no job is running, or accept that the test and the jobs slow each other.
To run the Disk Speed Test, do the following:
  1. Open Integrations, select DiskSpd and choose Run.
  2. In Preset, choose a KB2014 test for a repository or a source, or set your own mix of reads and writes, block size, threads and duration.
  3. In Where, choose the folder that holds the storage to test.
  4. In Used as, choose Backup repository, Backup source or Other.
  5. Choose Run. A question asks whether to start the test. On a backup server with Veeam jobs running, the question names the jobs and says that the test and the jobs slow each other: the result reads lower and the jobs take longer.
  6. Choose Yes. The result lists reads and writes apart in MB/s and GB/s, what SAT did and what it means for the role, then the full results.
  7. Choose CLI to see the command line that repeats the test.

Command line: storage tests and storage speed-test.

Related topics

Guided runsFile Transfer Calculator
Integrations > Database > Database console

Database console and guided query builder

The database console runs SQLCMD or psql in a window of its own, with a transcript, an input box and a guided query builder. Use it to run a query against Veeam's database, including a query that changes data. SQL Tools runs queries that read data only.

Before You Begin

  • Acquire SQLCMD or psql on Integrations first. See Acquiring a tool.
  • Veeam's default database is VeeamBackup.
  • A database password goes to the client through its environment, not on its command line, and does not appear in the transcript.

The connection fields

FieldWhat it does
Server or instanceThe server, local or a remote host. For SQLCMD the list holds the instances found by Find instances, as HOST\INSTANCE.
PortThe server's TCP port. Choosing an instance fills it.
DatabaseThe database to connect to. VeeamBackup is the default.
Sign in withThe current Windows account, or a database user. A database user takes User and Password.
To connect and run a query, do the following:
  1. Open Integrations, select SQLCMD or psql in the Database group and open its console.
  2. Fill Server or instance, Port and Database, and choose how to sign in in Sign in with.
  3. Choose Connect.
  4. Type the query in the input box and choose Send. The transcript shows what the client returns, with each result row on one line so the columns stay aligned. Scroll sideways to read a wide result. A divider between the transcript and the input box can be dragged.
  5. Choose Save output to write the transcript to a text file.
To find the SQL Server instances of a host, do the following:
  1. Open the SQLCMD console and type the host in Server or instance.
  2. Choose Find instances. SAT asks the SQL Server Browser on the host for its instances. Each fills the Server list as HOST\INSTANCE, with its version and TCP port in the transcript.
  3. Choose an instance. Port is filled in. A stopped Browser service or a firewall is reported, and the instance can still be typed.
To build a query, do the following:
  1. Choose Scan to list the tables of the connected database.
  2. Choose a table. SAT scans its columns. Choose a filter column; SAT scans the matching values of that column.
  3. Choose a comparison, a value, and a sort column and direction from the drop-downs.
  4. Choose the kind of query: SELECT, DELETE or UPDATE. The query is composed for one table, quoted for the engine, which matters for Veeam's PostgreSQL tables whose names contain dots, and placed in the input box.
  5. Review and edit the query, then choose Send.

Every field has hover text, and Tab moves between the fields.

Related topics

IntegrationsSQL ToolsAcquiring a tool
Integrations > Database > Database console > SQLCMD

SQLCMD

Microsoft's command-line client for SQL Server. Use it for a SQL Server configuration database or a Veeam plug-in's SQL Server. SAT finds it in an existing install, such as C:\Program Files\sqlcmd or the SQL Server Client SDK's ODBC Tools\Binn folder; otherwise Acquire downloads it. Its console has Find instances.

Before You Begin

  • SQLCMD has to be on this machine. With an engineer licence, Acquire downloads it; without one, Acquire names the official page and the folder to place it in.
  • Have the instance name as clients connect to it, and an account with access to it.
To open a SQLCMD console, do the following:
  1. Open Integrations and choose SQLCMD under Database.
  2. Choose Open console.
  3. In the connection bar, set the server, the database and how to sign in. Find instances lists the SQL Server instances that answer on the network.
  4. Choose Connect.
  5. Type a statement and choose Send.
Expected result. The transcript shows what the client returns. The password reaches the client through its environment and does not show in the transcript.

Related topics

Integrations > Database > Database console > psql (PostgreSQL)

psql (PostgreSQL)

PostgreSQL's command-line client. Use it for a PostgreSQL configuration database, port 5432 by default. SAT finds it in the PostgreSQL install folders (C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL\<version>\bin), including the PostgreSQL on a Veeam server; otherwise Acquire downloads it.

Before You Begin

  • psql has to be on this machine. With an engineer licence, Acquire downloads it; without one, Acquire names the official page and the folder to place it in.
  • Have the server name, the port and an account with access to the database.
To open a psql console, do the following:
  1. Open Integrations and choose psql (PostgreSQL) under Database.
  2. Choose Open console.
  3. In the connection bar, set the server, the port (5432 by default), the database and how to sign in.
  4. Choose Connect.
  5. Type a statement and choose Send.
Expected result. The transcript shows what the client returns. The password reaches the client through its environment and does not show in the transcript.

Database console and guided query builder
Application Reference > Settings

Settings

Settings holds the choices that apply to every case: the typeface and text size, the colour scheme, the default folders, case statuses and favourite SSH addresses. Open it with Tools > Settings....

The window has five tabs: General, Custom Statuses, SSH Addresses, Keyboard Shortcuts and About. Save applies the values immediately and, with an engineer licence, keeps them; the Settings window confirms on its own hint line. Defaults fills the General page with its defaults (UI font, text scale, colour scheme, the default folders and the tool-session limit) and keeps the engineer name; Save applies them.

General

SettingWhat it does
UI fontThe typeface used across the application, chosen from the fonts installed on this machine.
Text scale (%)Scales every piece of text together, 70 to 200, applied without restarting. Larger scales crowd the denser pages.
Colour schemeVeeam Green (the default), Dark, Light, or Match Windows, which follows the Windows app mode and changes with it. Applied to the open windows without a restart. The log viewer and the Remote (SSH) terminal keep their dark colours in every scheme.
Default engineer nameFills the Support Engineer field when you create a case.
Default collections folderWhere a new log collection starts.
Default case rootThe parent folder a new case workspace is created under.
Default tools folderThe managed folder used for tool downloads and capture output.
Maximum tool sessionsHow many tool tabs can be open at once, 1 to 30. Takes effect immediately.
Remote file pane widthWidth of the file pane on Remote (SSH), as a percentage of the page.

Without an engineer licence, a change saved in Settings applies until SAT closes and is not written anywhere. The same holds for the text scale, divider positions, panel sizes, custom statuses, SSH addresses and configured tools. With a licence they are kept in ApplicationLogs beside the executable, and activating a licence during a session keeps what that session changed. Recent Activity is recorded either way: each operation's time and outcome is kept in ApplicationLogs\activity.tsv as the history of the session, and a Customer / Lab collection carries it in the bundle.

Custom Statuses

Each row is a case status: a colour on the left and its name on the right. + Add status adds a row, Remove deletes one, and Save writes them. There are 24 colours; grey is the default. This replaces editing case-statuses.txt by hand.

SSH Addresses

Favourite lab hostnames or IPs. Save them here and pick one from the Host dropdown on Remote (SSH). The list holds addresses only; the account and password are entered per session.

Keyboard Shortcuts and About

The Keyboard Shortcuts tab lists the keys SAT answers. See Keyboard Shortcuts. The About tab shows the application identity and is read-only. Save is disabled on both tabs.

Procedures

To change how SAT looks, do the following:
  1. Choose Tools > Settings... and open the General tab.
  2. Choose a typeface in UI font, a size in Text scale (%) and a scheme in Colour scheme.
  3. Choose Save. The open windows change without a restart.
To set the default folders and engineer name, do the following:
  1. Open the General tab.
  2. Type the name in Default engineer name, and choose the folders in Default collections folder, Default case root and Default tools folder.
  3. Choose Save. Defaults fills the tab with its default values; Save applies them.
To add a case status, do the following:
  1. Open the Custom Statuses tab and choose + Add status.
  2. Choose the colour on the left and type the name on the right.
  3. Choose Save. The status appears in the Status dropdown of Case Manager.
To save a favourite SSH address, do the following:
  1. Open the SSH Addresses tab and add the hostname or IP address.
  2. Choose Save. The address appears in the Host dropdown on Remote (SSH).
Related topicsRemote (SSH)Help and F1About Cases
Application Reference > Keyboard Shortcuts

Keyboard Shortcuts

Keyboard Shortcuts lists every key SAT answers, by where it works. The list is on the Keyboard Shortcuts tab of Settings and in the tables below.

To look up a key, do the following:
  1. Choose Tools > Settings....
  2. Open the Keyboard Shortcuts tab. The keys are grouped by where they work: Anywhere in SAT, Quick tools, Log viewer, Remote (SSH) terminal, and Fields and tables.
To use a quick tool from the keyboard, do the following:
  1. Press the tool's key, for example F6 for the Local Port Checker. The tool opens in its own window in both roles.
  2. Press the key again while the window is open to bring that window to the front.

Anywhere in SAT

In every SAT window.

KeyAction
F1Help for this page. Opens the page's article in the Help window.
F5Refresh. Reloads the page in view.
Ctrl+KJump To. Finds a page, a tool, a case or a command as you type.
F11Full screen. Fills the screen; press it again to return.
Ctrl++Larger text. Ctrl+= works too. Up to 200%.
Ctrl+-Smaller text. Down to 70%.
Ctrl+0Text at 100%. Puts the text scale back.

Quick tools

Each opens its tool in a window of its own, in both roles, or brings that window to the front.

KeyAction
F2Name Check. What a name resolves to here, and where the answer came from.
F6Local Port Checker. Ports on this machine: the process on each, and the firewall's verdict.
F7Time Check. This clock against its time source, and a timestamp converter.
F8File Lock Check. Which process holds a file open, or anything under a folder.
F9Volume Check. Every volume, what it sits on, and whether Fast Clone can work there.
F10File Transfer Calculator. How long a transfer takes over a link, worked out step by step, with text for an email.
F12Service and Process Watch. Veeam's services and processes as they start, stop and end, with their ports.

F10 opens the File Transfer Calculator; Alt still opens the menu bar and Shift+F10 the context menu.

Log viewer

In a log opened from Log Review, Search Existing Logs or File Browser.

KeyAction
Ctrl+FFind. Opens the find box.
F3Next match. Enter in the find box does the same.
Shift+F3Previous match. Shift+Enter in the find box does the same.
EscClose find. Closes the find box.
Ctrl+GGo to line. Moves to a line number.
Alt+DownNext error or warning. Steps to the next line marked as an error or a warning.
Alt+UpPrevious error or warning. Steps back to the previous one.
Ctrl+MMark this value. Marks every occurrence of the value at the cursor. A double-click does the same.
Ctrl+Shift+MClear marks. Removes the marks.
Ctrl+BAdd to case. Adds the line to the active case.
Ctrl+HomeStart of the log. Moves to the first line.
Ctrl+EndEnd of the log. Moves to the last line.

Remote (SSH) terminal

While the terminal has the focus, every other key, function keys and Ctrl+K included, goes to the remote program.

KeyAction
Ctrl+Shift+CCopy. Copies the selected text.
Ctrl+Shift+VPaste. Types the clipboard into the remote program.
Ctrl+CInterrupt. Sent to the remote program, as in any terminal.

Fields and tables

Wherever there is a field, a list or a table.

Application Reference > Help and F1

Help and F1

Help is reached two ways: press F1 on any page for that page's article, or use the Help menu. F1 opens the article in its own Help window, so the page you were working on stays where it was. The Help window carries a topic dropdown, so you can move to another article without returning to the page.

An article is drawn as the cards are: sections of rows, each with its label and its text. In a tool's form or a Guided Diagnostics scenario's form, F1 opens that item's own article, the same as its card shows, as the first item of the topic dropdown. On other pages that item is not in the dropdown.

To open help for the page you are on, do the following:
  1. Press F1 on any page.
  2. The Help window opens on that page's article, for example File Browser, Remote (SSH), Log Review, or Integrations.
  3. Use the topic dropdown to read a different article, and leave the window open beside the page if it is useful.

The Help menu holds:

  • User Guide opens the shipped HTML guide for this version from the documents folder beside the application. It is greyed with (missing) if that file is not present.
  • Getting Started opens the quick-start article.
  • About SAT shows application identity and version, and the elevation, evidence-handling and privacy information.
  • Import Previous SAT Data reports what was migrated from an earlier layout and where it lives.

Version and build information

The rail shows the product version v0.5.0. Help > About SAT and the About tab of Settings show the application identity, and the version command prints the full version and the date the build was made.

Legacy SAT data import

When recognized older SAT-owned Logs, State, Tool-Output, or Tool-Outputs data needs to be retained, use the available legacy-path import/migration function. The source data is not automatically deleted after import. See Manual Upgrade before removing an older SAT folder.

Manual UpgradeFeedback and DebugTroubleshootingDownloading and Updating SAT
Application Reference > Feedback and Debug

Feedback and Debug

Feedback sends the SAT team a diagnostic package about SAT itself. Debug turns on additional logging for the session when SAT behaves unexpectedly.

Feedback

Feedback needs an engineer licence. Feedback prepares a SAT diagnostic package and opens the default mail application with the SAT feedback subject. The package holds SAT diagnostic information. It holds no copies of customer Veeam log bundles.

To send feedback, do the following:
  1. Choose Feedback in the status area.
  2. Wait for the default mail application to open with the SAT feedback subject.
  3. Add your comments and send the message.

Debug

Debug logging lasts for the session. Turn it on while troubleshooting SAT and off when the additional diagnostic output is not needed.

To turn debug logging on or off, do the following:
  1. Choose Debug in the status area.
  2. Choose it again to turn the logging off.

Command-Line Reference

SAT includes a command-line interface backed by the same shared core used by the Windows GUI. Run SupportAssistTool --help for the complete reference, which includes Windows command availability, required/optional values, defaults, permissions, exit codes, cancellation, output semantics, quoting and examples.

Runtime source of truth. Run SupportAssistTool --help on the target platform to see the command surface advertised by that build. Windows-only technologies are not advertised as Linux/macOS capabilities.

Application Reference > Troubleshooting

Troubleshooting

I do not have an Active case

Log Review and Universal Log Collection can be used in a No Case context for one-off customer/lab work. Create/select a case only when you want persistent parser/evidence/note state. See Collecting Without a Case and About Cases.

Log Review says INDEXED: PRELIMINARY

The initial Fast Index completed successfully but intentionally deferred deeper work. Select Complete full review when the current investigation requires the entire source set.

A machine shows an unexpected product

Use Product Identification and compare the selected machine/source with the strongest source signatures. Remember that one machine can contain several product roles. See Product Context and Terminology.

A finding is not attached to a run

Some service/background/infrastructure symptoms do not contain enough evidence to bind safely to one job run. Review them in All Machines or Machine Activity without assuming a run.

A finding has no parsed timestamp

SAT keeps raw source timestamp information when available and places unknown/unparsed timestamps below timestamped items in broad views. See Sorting and Chronology.

A saved Health Monitor snapshot will not load

Verify that you selected the SAT-generated Health Monitor snapshot from the collection. General text without the SAT health-data section cannot be reconstructed as a saved snapshot. See Reviewing a Saved Health Snapshot.

UDP reports Indeterminate / No Response

This is expected when SAT can send the datagram but no application response is received. Use a cooperating SAT UDP Listener for a verified probe/ACK.

TCP connects but the payload validation fails

The socket path accepted a connection, but the bounded SAT-to-SAT transfer did not complete/verify. Review the failure point, interface/route, listener result, and Test ID. Continue with Testing Across Local Interfaces or packet capture when the investigation requires it.

One TLS version fails

When comparing TLS 1.2/1.3, treat a disabled or unavailable version as an observed configuration/negotiation result. Compare the result with current product/security policy and the Veeam documentation in Related Documentation.

The certificate step reads MISMATCH

Compare the expected certificate's source with the certificate the target presented. Confirm the intended endpoint and follow the current Veeam certificate procedure before changing a certificate. See Certificate or TLS error between Veeam components.

A tool or Guided Diagnostic is not shown

A platform-wide category can show an unavailable or not-applicable state when the current operating system cannot run that operation. Product-specific diagnostics can also be hidden when the required local Veeam role is not detected. Run the diagnostic on the customer/lab host where the applicable product/component exists. See Supported Platforms and Availability.

Environment Review is still collecting a section

Some environment categories take longer to query than others. Completed sections remain usable while later read-only queries continue. If a section cannot be collected, SAT reports it as unavailable or warning.

VSS does not proceed past administrator approval

Review the live VSS lifecycle row. SAT reports when approval is being requested, when the elevated helper connects, and when VSS initialization begins. If UAC is declined, the operation stops before creating a snapshot. If another SAT instance is already running a stateful VSS diagnostic, finish/cancel that operation before starting another.

VSS reports Cleanup needs review

SAT deletes only the snapshot set it created, then rechecks those exact snapshot IDs during a short verification window. A warning means SAT could not establish the terminal absent state. Do not delete unrelated snapshots based only on this message; preserve the SAT lifecycle output and continue with the normal VSS investigation.

Environment Review reports OS default for TLS

An absent SCHANNEL override is not automatically the same as Disabled. Treat OS-default, explicitly enabled, explicitly disabled, unsupported and unavailable states as different evidence and compare them with the current Windows/Veeam policy for the affected product.

A collection shows Warning/Error but no source line opens

Double-click the result row. When the row has no openable source-file/line reference, SAT opens the complete recorded row detail.

A Windows Event Log folder is empty

Review the collection result warnings/details. SAT exports selected channels through the native Event Log API and records the Windows error code when export/archive fails. Do not treat an empty directory as a successful Event Log capture without checking those results.

Introduction > What’s New in v0.5.0

What’s New in v0.5.0

Support Assist Tool 0.5.0 is the first release of the 0.5 line, the Beta. The tools are grouped by category, Guided Diagnostics works by symptom, SQL Tools checks a server against Veeam's requirements, and System Differences shows what changed on a machine. Upgrading from 0.4.x keeps your cases. Earlier versions are listed in Release History.

New Features

  • Home. Home is a status board. In Engineer Review it follows the active case through its steps, with the next steps, the running jobs and the cases opened most recently. In Customer / Lab it shows this machine's health, the Veeam products and services found, and this session's collections and output. See Home.
  • Tools by category. A tile for each category leads its Tools page. Each tool opens on a card with what it does, an OPTIONS line for each field and tick box, and the button that runs it. See Tools Overview.
  • Guided Diagnostics. Scenarios by symptom, such as a managed server that cannot be reached, a certificate or TLS error between Veeam components, a SQL transaction log backup that fails, or a slow backup. The steps run in order and stop at the first one that decides the case; each step says what it means and where the rule comes from. See Guided Diagnostics Overview.
  • SQL Tools. Five read-only checks: Permission check, which holds an account's rights against Veeam's lists for guest processing or the configuration database; Server shape; Backups and log chain; Database files and volumes; and Read-only query. Engine chooses SQL Server, read over ODBC, or PostgreSQL, read through psql. Use logged-in user signs in as you; otherwise SAT asks for a SQL login, kept for the run only. See SQL Tools.
  • The log chain in Backups and log chain. Below the findings, every backup in msdb's history, oldest first, with its place in the chain: OK, Base, Base changed, Lost, After loss, New chain or Gap before. Each backup names who took it. A log backup to NUL reads Fail; a full that is not copy-only beside Veeam reads Attention; the first log backup after a new database's first full backup is not reported as a restart.
  • System Differences. Replaces Filesystem Change and Registry Change. The Files and Registry cards each open a page with Capture, Compare and Open:
    • Capture what is there, make the change, then Compare with Now or with a second capture. Compare takes the capture first when there is none yet.
    • Every compare is kept in the capture file. Open lists the capture, its compares, newest first, and its files and folders.
    • As administrator, a files capture reads the folder from the NTFS master file table and records where the NTFS change journal stands. The compare then lists files created and removed in between, and files renamed. Without administrator, Capture asks to run as administrator, and the result line says how the folder was read.
    • Registry scope takes a key or a whole hive: HKLM, HKU, HKCR, HKCC or HKCU.
    See System Differences.
  • Named Pipes. On Host Diagnostics: every pipe in \\.\pipe\ with its instances, and the pipes of Veeam products, SQL Server and PostgreSQL named with their service. See Named Pipes.
  • Host Checks. On Host Diagnostics: backup events (volsnap, VSS, disk and NTFS), the Veeam drivers, VSS shadow storage, and the .NET and TLS settings, a tick box each. See Host Checks.
  • Installer Cache Check. On Host Diagnostics: the installed Veeam products with their original packages, the cached package Windows keeps in C:\Windows\Installer, present or missing, and their patches. Check reads an .msi, an .exe or a folder such as a mounted ISO, and says whether an .msi is the package a product was installed from. See Installer Cache Check.
  • WMI Health. On WMI Diagnostics: this machine's WMI service and the services it needs, the repository's consistency and size, a timed probe of each namespace Veeam reads, and the WMI faults Windows logged. See WMI Health.
  • Veeam Service Channel. On Network Tools: the channel Veeam Agent's processes use to reach their service, tested as the service, its named pipe, an HTTP/2 handshake on it and the gRPC lines the product logged. See Veeam Service Channel.
  • Quick tools. Name Check (F2), Local Port Checker (F6), Time Check (F7), File Lock Check (F8), Volume Check (F9), File Transfer Calculator (F10) and Service and Process Watch (F12), each in its own window, in both roles. The newest run of each shows in Environment Review and Health Monitor, and Log Collection gathers them. See About the quick tools.
  • Packet capture. One tool on Network Tools: Start capture, then Stop capture, which converts the capture to PCAPNG. While it runs the packets are counted every 5 seconds. After Stop the notable events are listed: retransmissions, duplicate acknowledgements, resets, zero windows, missing segments, and TLS handshake messages and alerts. See Packet Capture.
  • Process Monitor capture. Start capture and Stop capture beside Launch on Integrations. See About Integrations.
  • Disk Speed Test. KB2014's storage tests on DiskSpd, run from Integrations, with the results read for the storage's role. See Disk Speed Test.
  • Requirements on Diagnostics. .NET, Windows PowerShell and PowerShell 7, the execution policy, the Windows build, the service manager, the WMI service, administrator rights, the SQL Server ODBC drivers and psql, listed after the SAT Self-Test. See Diagnostics.

Tool Updates

  • Read-only query. The result is a grid of the main columns, one line per result row, with a divider and, under it, a pane holding every value of the selected row. The tool output keeps it as query.tsv as well. The Query field keeps the name of a named query. After a run the form folds and Run query is hidden until Edit.
    • Edit query... beside Query opens a window with an example that lists the chosen database's tables, or the field's own query, and says which database it runs in. Run query puts the query in the field on one line and runs it.
    • A query that could change data is not run. The tab's output shows one row with the query, Not run, the reason and Fail, the status line reads Not run with the reason in plain English, no SQL login is asked for, and the window stays open with the reason under the box. Changes are made in the database console, with sqlcmd or psql.
    • The named queries include Backup audit (this database) for SQL Server, which takes backup_type first, and Backup readiness (WAL archiving and slots) for PostgreSQL. Each result row is named by its database.
  • Local Port Checker. The list is read again while the window is open, takes port ranges such as 22-23, and shows loopback ports. Export... saves the ports as CSV or JSON. The presets list the ports of VBR 12 and VBR 13 and mark a port that only one version lists: VBR 12 only, VBR 13 only. See Local Port Checker (F6).
  • Guided Diagnostics. A scenario ends with a case note block, and a step that was not checked reads Attention. The managed-server scenario has an optional VBR version input, 12 or 13: left empty it tests the ports of both and names the version of each port only one version lists. See Guided Diagnostics Overview.
  • Remote Port Checker. TCP / UDP Connectivity is the Remote Port Checker. It shows where the name resolved from, an IPv4 and an IPv6 row, and each address, sent from the adapters chosen in Send from these adapters.
  • Health Monitor. Reads the event logs for disk and file system errors, shows each adapter's link speed and MTU and each volume's sector size, partition style and driver, and rates memory on the memory free. The tables size their columns to their text and scroll sideways.
  • WMI Diagnostics. A query to another machine shows its stages as rows while it runs: Connect, Query and Read rows. WMI Health checks this machine and has no Machine field. Process Inventory is on Host Diagnostics. One row per object with its properties together. A namespace the machine does not have, such as root\MSCluster without the failover cluster role, is a result. The WQL field offers example queries for the namespace chosen. WMI Cluster Diagnostics and Custom WMI Query take a machine name, with this machine first in the list.
  • Sign in to another machine. WMI Cluster Diagnostics and Custom WMI Query sign in to another machine as the account SAT runs as, or as another account that Windows' sign-in dialog asks for at Query. The account is used for that query and not saved, and the connection is encrypted.
  • Database console. Labelled connection fields, Find instances, which lists a host's SQL Server instances, and a divider between the transcript and the query box.
  • Installer Cache Check. The Installer registry keys fill a value the Windows Installer leaves empty, and give a product's upgrade code.
  • iPerf3. The Run window has the presets Veeam default: five streams for a minute and Like a restore: five streams back to this machine, and Number of streams is 5. See Guided runs.
  • Disk Speed Test. On a backup server the start question names the Veeam jobs running and says that the test and the jobs slow each other. The Run window shows the command line for the test. See Disk Speed Test.
  • VSS Tools. Choose... beside Writer class GUIDs lists the writers found, to tick.
  • Environment Review. A section's rows show as a grid with a column per field, and Quick checks lists the kept quick tool runs.
  • Recent Activity. Tiles for all entries, findings, failures and cancels that filter the list, short results, and a collected record opened in place of this machine's.
  • Log Review. Engineer Review Home's third tile is Evidence, the log lines kept as evidence. The choice for logs from several Veeam products, or a product with no parser of its own, is Generic Parser.
  • File Transfer Calculator. Manual and Live test modes, sizes from MB to PB, and every estimate recorded in Recent Activity.

User Interface

  • Feedback. Feedback needs an engineer licence.
  • Help. Articles are drawn as cards, and F1 in a tool's or a scenario's form opens that item's own article.
  • Progress. The running bar fills to the percent when a tool knows how far it is, and the status line gives the time left. Log Review and Log Collection list each file or step as they reach it, Current then Done.
  • Fields that offer values. Port, Host, Days, From and To, UTC offset, Compare file contents, Registry scope, WMI namespace and Database fields list their values at the field. Host fields list the active case's machines and the addresses saved in Settings.
  • Tables. A table sizes its columns to their contents, and the spare width goes to the widest column. A column you drag keeps its width until new rows arrive.
  • Tools output. After a run the form folds, and the table shows the result with a pane under it for the selected row. Edit opens the form again.
  • Compact cards. On a short window the cards on Home and the review pages show compact, so the page stays in view.
  • Full screen. F11 fills the screen and the Exit full screen button returns to the window.
  • Recent cases. Home lists the cases opened most recently, and a deleted case leaves Home and Case Manager at once.
  • Links in this guide. A link to a heading inside another article opens that article at the heading.

Command Line

  • sql query prints its statement first, then a table or a block per row; --format table|records|tsv, and --query takes a named query's name.
  • sql check, shape, backups, files and query, with --engine postgres and --show-sql; sql instances and sql databases.
  • guided scenarios and guided run; system host-checks; system installer-cache; wmi health; network service-channel; packet events.
  • files compare and registry compare take --keep, which keeps the compare in the capture file, and baseline inspect lists a capture's compares and how it was read.
  • diagnostics prints the requirements.
  • system pipes lists the named pipes; network presets marks the ports only VBR 12 or only VBR 13 lists; guided run --input vbr_version=12 sets the VBR version of a scenario; logs universal includes the kept tool output.
  • wmi query --user signs in to another machine as another account, with the password read from SAT_WMI_PASSWORD.

See the CLI User Guide.

Security and Downloads

  • Libraries. OpenSSL 3.5.9 and libarchive 3.8.10.
  • Tool downloads. The download links are part of SAT, and every downloaded program is checked against its publisher's signature, or iPerf3's and psql's against a pinned SHA-256, before it reaches the Tools folder. Without a licence SAT opens the tool's page for a manual download. See Acquiring a tool.
  • Remote work over SSH. WinRM Remote is removed; remote work runs on Remote (SSH).
  • Administrator work. Log Collection, packet capture, the VSS test and a System Differences capture run as administrator through SAT's elevated helper after one Windows approval, while SAT itself stays a standard process.

Bug Fixes

  • A compare of a folder with 300,000 objects finishes in seconds and stops on Cancel.
  • A registry compare stops on Cancel.
  • Captures, compares and reviews work in folders named in any language, such as Japanese or Polish.
  • A whole volume, such as C:\, can be captured, and a registry value with no data is captured as empty.
  • A WMI query of a namespace missing on another machine names that machine.
